809.author: HugoXK
809.body:
## What happens

A JSON artifact whose document carries an integer above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` is shown with a **different value** in the preview. The table cell and both text views go through IEEE-754 doubles, so the digits are replaced by the nearest representable neighbour.

Reproduced on `main` at `8708320f80af8a72ea96653e2a71bd89d83a6850` against `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (probe drives the real `buildArtifactVersionPreview`, fake store/recorder only supply the stored bytes):

```
# TABLE {"mode":"dataset-table","columns":["sample_id","label"],"rows":[["9007199254740992","x"]],"raw":"[\\n  {\\n    \\"sample_id\\": 9007199254740992,\\n    \\"label\\": \\"x\\"\\n  }\\n]"}
# RAW "[\\n  {\\n    \\"sample_id\\": 9007199254740992\\n  }\\n]"
# SOURCE {"mode":"json-source","source":"{\\n  \\"run_id\\": 12345678901234567000\\n}","parsed":true}
not ok 1 - a record table keeps an integer id above 2^53 exact
  expected: '9007199254740993'
  actual: '9007199254740992'
not ok 2 - the raw JSON view keeps an integer id above 2^53 exact
  expected: true
  actual: false
not ok 3 - a scalar-id document keeps its literal digits in the JSON source view
  expected: true
  actual: false
# tests 3
# pass 0
# fail 3
```

Input documents: `[{"sample_id":9007199254740993,"label":"x"}]` and `{"run_id":12345678901234567890}`.

## Why it matters

Sample, run and registration identifiers routinely exceed 2^53. The viewer shows `...992` for `...993`, and the "Raw JSON" pane re-serialises the same wrong value, so the user copies a plausible but different identifier into their analysis. The same data stored as `.csv` goes through the string path and stays exact, so the two previews of one value disagree.

## Where

`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (display layer only):

- `recordArrayTable` — the table cell is `String(value)`, after the document was parsed into doubles.
- `buildJsonPreview` — `rawJson` is `JSON.stringify(parsed, null, 2)`, i.e. re-serialised from the rounded value.
- `buildJsonPreview` — the `json-source` fallback is `JSON.stringify(parsed, null, 2)` too.

## Expected

- A record array keeps each integer literal exactly as written: the cell for `9007199254740993` reads `9007199254740993`.
- `rawJson.source` and the `json-source` view echo the stored document (BOM-stripped the same way #805 does), not a re-serialisation, so both stay exact.
- Ordinary values do not regress: `42` still renders as `42`, strings and nested objects unchanged, and the existing `dashboard.test.ts` cases stay green.

## Scope / non-goals

- One file, `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`. No change to `packages/artifact-manager`, the job shape, the CAS or the stored artifact.
- The UTF-8 BOM handling added by #805 stays exactly as it is; this is about numeric literals, not the leading marker.
- The CSV/TSV path is out of scope (it already yields strings).
- If the fix turns out to need a change outside this file, stop and report instead of widening the PR.
809.title: JSON artifact preview silently rewrites integers above 2^53

812.author: wyhohyw
812.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Scientific self-evolution here is two loops, and only the inner one is in scope for this issue. The inner loop improves the result of the current run: Evolve proposes a candidate, a scene executes it, the score is read from outside the candidate, and the loop repeats until the budget or a stop rule. The outer loop, later, turns a validated rule or program into something the next run can use. An inner winner is not published just because this run scored well. That outer loop, the antibody chain, and skill-library publish are not this issue.

This issue adds two capabilities to the Evolve that already ships on `main`. It does not replace that Evolve.

1. Evolve can run an NPU evaluation. The search stays next to the API: it proposes candidates and keeps the archive. Each candidate that needs this conversation's runner is scored in a sandbox created on that runner. The sandbox has no network. The cards the operator already selected are attached only when this score needs them. Submit, wait, recover, cancel, and the result use the existing shell-execution path. A search that does not use a runner keeps today's local sandbox, and that local sandbox is not given a network or a card.
2. A search can be directed. The thing being changed is a JSON object, not the pipeline. The scorecard names the fields a candidate may change. Anything else is not a legal candidate. A search that does not declare a direction stays the free program search that exists today.

The behavior of today's Evolve is the baseline. A scorecard, script, judge, or test-gate search that does not ask for these two capabilities must keep its current results, sandbox, and stop rules. New behavior is selected only by the scorecard. Weakening an existing test to make the new path fit is a failed change.

No stand-in model, scene name, sequence, or example metric belongs in product code, unit tests, or system tests. If a short scene later proves useful, it may be added only as its own end-to-end case, in a later change. It is not part of this issue's implementation, and it is not a unit or system test.

Evolve today ranks candidates through a `Domain` (`vendor/puct/domain.py`: initial program, `evaluate`, `reward`, rewrite prompt, metric name). `scorecard_domain.py` already plugs a task into that seam. The local candidate sandbox (`vendor/puct/sandbox.py`) stays the right confinement for short untrusted programs that do not need the runner: Bubblewrap or Seatbelt, no network, writes only in scratch, CPU and memory limits, one thread, no accelerator. `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` locks that behavior in. A long NPU job does not fit inside that local sandbox, and giving every local candidate a network or a card would weaken that confinement without putting the job on the machine that has the card. The score that needs the card runs on the selected runner, in a sandbox that still has no network.

The same `Domain` can also rewrite a whole program. A scientific scene has a legal direction. Only fields the scene declares may change. Unknown fields fail closed. A missing result is not stored as `0`, because `0` would rank a failed job as a real score. `script_domain.py` is the wrong mode for the NPU path: it lets the model write the scorer. Prompt text is not the enforcement either. The program that computes the score is fixed and runs on the runner. The candidate only supplies the fields it is allowed to change. A number the candidate prints is not the score.

## Design Ideas

- **Today's Evolve stays the default.** PUCT, OpenEvolve, the existing `Domain` seam, and the four current measurement kinds stay. A search with no NPU measure and no `direction` follows the code path it follows on `main` now. `vendor/puct/search.py` is not rewritten, and the default local sandbox profile is not edited.
- **The NPU score runs on the selected runner.** The search loop stays beside the API, because it calls the model and writes the archive on the disk the API reads. One candidate is one shell execution, with its own execution id, on the runner this conversation selected. The runner creates the sandbox. The sandbox has no network. The cards already selected for that runner are bound only when this score needs them. Weights stay on the runner and are read by the fixed program. The candidate JSON is sent with the execution. Success is `completed`, not `succeeded`. Queue time counts toward that job's own time limit. At the limit, the job is cancelled. A search that names no runner does not submit a remote execution.
- **No silent CPU fallback.** If the device is not NPU, the job is a failure. `device` must be `npu`. A detector that falls through to CUDA or CPU must not be reused here.
- **The scene declares the legal move.** `direction.editable` lists the only top-level fields that may differ from the baseline JSON object. A candidate that is not that object, or that changes any other field, adds a field, or removes a field, is `valid=False`. It is not given a low score. A position inside one string cannot be locked on its own: that position has to be its own field. With no `direction`, the search remains free, as it is today.
- **Where the JSON comes from, and how the user sees it.** The JSON comes from the workspace when the user already has one. Otherwise the agent drafts it from the conversation and shows it before the run starts. The user corrects it in the conversation. The screen does not show the raw JSON. Before the run it shows a table. Each row has the field name, the current value, and whether this run may change it. The user ticks the rows, then agrees to start. A long value shows its beginning; the full value opens on click. The ticked rows are `direction.editable`. While the run is going, each row shows the field that changed, the old value, the new value, and the score. After the run has started, the search changes the ticked fields. The user is not asked to edit each try.
- **Seen edits and fault retries stay bounded.** An edit that was already kept is not a new node. Returning to a seen edit whose score does not improve on the score already stored for it is not adopted. Fault, cancel, and missing-artifact retries of the same edit are capped and do not spend another search slot. Waiting is not a fault and does not spend another slot. The guard does not generate the next candidate and does not reimplement the tree.
- **Three job states stay distinct.** Not finished (`queued`, `running`, `unknown`): wait, score empty. Failed, cancelled, or missing artifact: fault, score empty, never `0`. A valid NPU result: record the metric, including a genuinely low one. One card runs a limited number of jobs. The search may keep proposing. Scoring waits on the runner's queue. Waiting does not spend a second slot.

**Where a candidate runs**

| | Today on `main` | After this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Search | Next to the API. It proposes candidates and keeps the archive. | Same place. |
| Score that does not need a runner | Local sandbox. No network. No card. | Same local sandbox. |
| Score that needs the selected runner | Still the local sandbox. That sandbox cannot see the card. | One sandbox per candidate on that runner. No network. The selected cards are attached only when this score needs them. |
| Who computes the score | The measurement outside the candidate, for today's modes. | A fixed program on the runner. The candidate supplies the JSON. A number the candidate prints is not the score. |

**What the search is allowed to change**

| | Today on `main` | After this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Starting point | A program. | A JSON object. |
| What the model may rewrite | The whole program. | Only the named fields. |
| Before scoring | The candidate is scored as it is. | The candidate is compared with the starting point, field by field. |
| An unnamed field changed | It is still scored. | Rejected. No score. |
| A field added or removed | It is still scored. | Rejected. No score. |
| No field list | The whole program may be rewritten. | Still the whole program. This check is not applied. |

**Example input**

The pipeline stays as it is. Each round sends one JSON object into that same pipeline. The fixed program reads the object and returns the score.

Starting point:

```json
{
  "pos_2": "T",
  "pos_4": "K",
  "model": "fixed"
}
```

Fields this run may change: `pos_2`, `pos_4`.

A legal candidate. Only `pos_2` changed. This one is scored:

```json
{
  "pos_2": "A",
  "pos_4": "K",
  "model": "fixed"
}
```

Changing `model`, adding a field, removing a field, or replacing the object with a program does not get a score. On the confirmation screen this object is the table: three rows, and the user ticks `pos_2` and `pos_4`.

Alternatives considered and rejected: allowing network and devices inside every local candidate sandbox (breaks the confinement tests and gives untrusted code the accelerator); moving the whole search into that no-network sandbox (the search has to call the model, and the archive has to stay where the API can read it); treating "only edit these fields" as prompt text (the model can ignore it); letting the candidate report its own score; putting a particular model or scene into the product modules or into unit and system tests (that scene is not this change).

## Involved Public APIs

No new public HTTP API. The domain seam is unchanged: `evaluate(code, shards) -> (valid, metrics, error)`. The NPU path reuses the existing shell execution routes on the conversation's selected runner (`POST /shell-executions`, status, logs, cancel). The API already selects that runner and signs the request. Any change to those routes must keep current skill launches, including the antibody pipeline and CodonTransformer, behaving as they do now.

The new behavior is opt-in on the existing engines: a score that uses the selected runner, and an optional `direction` object taken from the fields the user ticked. The confirmation before the run shows the field table. This issue does not add a model-specific domain, skill, or fixture.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `services/evolve`: add the opt-in runner evaluation and the direction check. Existing measurement kinds keep their current behavior. Do not edit `vendor/puct/search.py` or the default local sandbox profile.
- `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py`: remains the lock on the local confinement. This issue is not done if those tests are weakened so that ordinary candidates can see the network or an accelerator.
- The evolve confirmation and the run panel: the field table before the run, and the old-value / new-value / score rows while it runs. Raw JSON is not that view.
- Skill execution: an NPU search uses the same shell-execution contract as the current NPU skills, including the runner sandbox and the already selected cards. It does not call `run_npu_job`.
- Antibody skills and MindSpore operators are not modified. An NPU job completing does not certify RFdiffusion, ProteinMPNN, or Protenix.
- Skill-library publish, replay, and the outer loop are out of scope. This issue must not write an inner winner into the skill library.

## Test Design and Test Plan

Default CI does not need an Ascend device. Tests use a runner double that speaks the shell-execution states. They do not name a model, load weights, or embed a scene. Unit tests and system tests stay free of any stand-in model. An end-to-end case, if one is justified later, is a separate change and is not part of `pnpm evolve:test`.

- **Unit, NPU job.** A completed record with `device=npu` returns `valid=True` and the metric from that record. The metric is the number returned by the fixed program. A number printed by the candidate is not stored. A queued, running, or unknown record, a missing artifact, a non-`npu` device, and a failed or cancelled execution each return `valid=False` with an empty score, not `0`. Each candidate is its own execution id. The unit test does not import a model runtime.
- **Unit, direction.** An unknown field is rejected. A change to a field that is not in `direction.editable` is rejected. A free-form program is rejected when a direction is set. A scorecard with no direction is not passed through this check. A previously seen edit that does not improve is not a new node. Fault retries stop at the cap and do not spend another search slot; waiting does not.
- **Unit, sandbox regression.** `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` stays as it is: network denied, writes confined to scratch, no backend refuses to run unconfined, CPU budget floor unchanged. Constructing the NPU path does not flip the default local sandbox to allow network or devices. A search with no runner does not submit a remote execution.
- **The field table.** Before the run, the confirmation shows the field name, the current value, and a tick for whether this run may change it. During the run, a row shows the changed field, the old value, the new value, and the score. A long value shows its beginning until opened.
- **Regression, the baseline.** Existing scorecard, PUCT fidelity, script-domain, judge, and test-gate tests pass without changing their assertions. That is the proof that today's Evolve still behaves as it does on `main`. The antibody pipeline tests are not part of this issue and must not be edited to go green.
- **Not in unit or system tests.** No model-specific forward, fixture sequence, or scene skill. Hardware smoke, if it is ever run, is reported separately and is not folded into `pnpm evolve:test`.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm evolve:test`, with the same pass and skip counts the unmodified `main` suite has, plus the new tests above. A machine without an accelerator still passes that command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An Evolve search that does not request an NPU job and does not set `direction` behaves as it does on `main`, including the current local sandbox. `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` passes without allowing network or devices for every candidate. Existing Evolve tests pass without assertion edits.
- [ ] A search that uses the conversation's runner scores each candidate in a sandbox on that runner. The sandbox has no network. Cards are attached only when the score needs them. The search itself stays next to the API.
- [ ] An NPU evaluation scores only a completed `device=npu` result returned by the fixed program, and never writes `0` for a waiting, failed, cancelled, or missing result. It does not fall back to CPU or CUDA. Queue time counts toward that job's limit, and the job is cancelled at the limit.
- [ ] When `direction.editable` is set, a candidate outside those fields is rejected before scoring. When it is absent, the search stays free.
- [ ] Before the run, the user sees a table of field name, current value, and whether this run may change it, and ticks the rows. The raw JSON is not that view. During the run, each row shows the changed field, the old value, the new value, and the score.
- [ ] Product code, unit tests, and system tests contain no stand-in model, scene skill, or scene fixture. A later end-to-end case is out of this issue.
- [ ] `vendor/puct/search.py` is unchanged. No second search implementation lands under `skills/`.
- [ ] `pnpm evolve:test` passes. The inner result is not published to the skill library.

## Additional Information

Final scientific acceptance of the two-loop design remains a full antibody design run and is not an acceptance line of this issue.

## 🚀 背景描述

这里的科研自进化是两层循环。本 issue 只做内层。内层改进这一次 Run 的结果：Evolve 提出候选，场景执行，分数在候选程序外面读取，直到预算用尽或触发停止。外层以后才把经过独立验证的规则或程序交给后续 Run。内层赢家不能因为这一次分高就发布。外层、抗体设计链和技能库发布都不在本 issue 里。

本 issue 在 `main` 上已有的 Evolve 里加两件事，不换成另一套 Evolve。

1. Evolve 能跑 NPU 评分。搜索留在 API 旁边：它提出候选、保存档案。要用本轮对话选中的 Runner 时，每个候选在那台机器上的沙箱里评分。沙箱不上网。只有这次评分要用卡时，才把操作者已经勾选的卡放进去。提交、等待、恢复、取消和结果回传走现有的 Shell 执行路径。没有使用 Runner 的搜索仍用今天的本机沙箱，这个本机沙箱不获得网络，也不获得卡。
2. 搜索可以定向。被修改的是一份 JSON，不是整条流程。scorecard 声明候选可以改哪些字段。其余改动不是合法候选。没有声明方向的搜索，仍是现在这种自由的程序搜索。

今天 Evolve 的行为就是基线。没有要求这两项能力的 scorecard、脚本、评审或测试门搜索，必须保持现在的结果、沙箱和停止规则。新行为只由 scorecard 选中。为了让新路径通过而放宽已有测试，算失败。

正式代码、单元测试和系统测试里不放替身模型、场景名、序列或示例指标。如果以后某条短场景确实有用，只能在另一次改动里作为端到端用例加入。它不是本 issue 的实现，也不是单元测试或系统测试。

现有 Evolve 通过 `Domain` 给候选排序（`vendor/puct/domain.py`：起点程序、`evaluate`、`reward`、改写提示、指标名）。`scorecard_domain.py` 已经按这条缝接入。不需要 Runner 的短程序，仍用本机候选沙箱（`vendor/puct/sandbox.py`）：Bubblewrap 或 Seatbelt、无网络、只能写临时目录、有 CPU 和内存上限、单线程、没有加速器。`tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` 把这些行为锁住了。一次长的 NPU 作业不该塞进这个本机沙箱。给所有本机候选放开网络或发一张卡，会削弱这层隔离，作业也仍然不在有卡的那台机器上。需要卡的评分在选中的 Runner 上跑，那个沙箱同样不上网。

同一个 `Domain` 现在还可以改写整个程序。科学场景有合法方向。场景没有声明的字段不能改。未知字段直接失败。没有结果不能记成 `0`，否则失败作业会变成一个真实分数。`script_domain.py` 不适用于 NPU 这条路径，它让模型自己写评分程序。只在提示词里要求“只改这些字段”也不算约束。算分的程序是固定的，跑在 Runner 上。候选只提供允许改的字段。候选自己打印的数字不算分数。

## 设计思路

- **今天的 Evolve 仍是默认路径。** PUCT、OpenEvolve、现有 `Domain` 缝和现有四种评分方式都保留。没有 NPU 评分、也没有 `direction` 的搜索，走它现在在 `main` 上的路径。不改写 `vendor/puct/search.py`，也不改默认的本机沙箱配置。
- **NPU 评分在选中的 Runner 上跑。** 搜索循环留在 API 旁边，因为它要调用模型，档案也要写在 API 能读到的那块磁盘上。一个候选是一次 Shell 执行，有自己的执行编号，发到本轮对话选中的 Runner。沙箱由这台 Runner 创建。沙箱不上网。这台 Runner 上已经勾选的卡，只有这次评分需要时才绑进去。权重留在 Runner 上，由固定程序去读。候选 JSON 随这次执行送过去。成功状态是 `completed`，不是 `succeeded`。排队时间算进这次作业自己的时限。到点就取消。没有指定 Runner 的搜索不提交远程执行。
- **禁止悄悄退回 CPU。** 设备不是 NPU 时，作业失败。`device` 必须是 `npu`。会落到 CUDA 或 CPU 的探测不能用在这里。
- **场景声明合法动作。** `direction.editable` 列出相对基线 JSON 可以不同的最外层字段。候选不是这个对象，或者改了别的字段、多了字段、少了字段，就是 `valid=False`，不给一个低分代替。写在同一个字符串里的某一个位置不能单独锁住，这个位置必须自成一个字段。没有 `direction` 时，搜索仍是现在这种自由搜索。
- **JSON 从哪来，用户怎么看。** 用户已经有 JSON，就用工作区里的那份。没有的话，Agent 按对话写一份初稿，开始前给用户看。用户在对话里改。界面不直接显示原始 JSON。开始前用一张表，每一行是字段名、当前值、这次能不能改。用户勾选能改的几行，再同意开始。值太长时先显示开头，点开看全文。勾中的行就是 `direction.editable`。运行中，每一行显示改了哪一项、旧值、新值、多少分。运行开始以后，搜索去改勾中的字段。不会让用户逐次去改。
- **见过的修改和失败重试都有界。** 已经收成节点的修改不再是新节点。改回已经见过的修改时，分数没有超过该修改已记下的成绩，也不收成新节点。同一次修改因失败、取消或产物缺失而重试时有次数上限，并且不再另占一个搜索名额。等待不是失败，也不另占名额。这层检查不生成下一轮候选，也不重写树搜索。
- **三种作业状态分开。** 未结束（`queued`、`running`、`unknown`）：等待，分数为空。失败、取消或产物缺失：故障，分数为空，不写 `0`。有效的 NPU 结果：记下指标，哪怕这个指标确实很低。一张卡同时能跑的作业有限。搜索可以继续提议。评分排在 Runner 的队列后面。等待不再占第二个名额。

**候选在哪里跑**

| | 现在的 `main` | 这次改完之后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 搜索 | 在 API 旁边。它提出候选、保存档案。 | 还在这里。 |
| 不需要 Runner 的评分 | 本机沙箱。不上网。没有卡。 | 仍是这个本机沙箱。 |
| 需要选中 Runner 的评分 | 仍在本机沙箱。这个沙箱看不见那张卡。 | 每个候选在那台 Runner 上单独一个沙箱。不上网。这次评分要用卡，才绑已经勾选的卡。 |
| 谁算分 | 现有几种评分在候选外面算。 | Runner 上的固定程序算。候选只提供 JSON。候选自己打印的数字不算分。 |

**搜索可以改什么**

| | 现在的 `main` | 这次改完之后 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 起点 | 一段程序。 | 一份 JSON。 |
| 模型可以改什么 | 整段程序。 | 只改点名的字段。 |
| 评分前 | 直接拿去评分。 | 先和起点逐项对照。 |
| 没点名的字段变了 | 照样评分。 | 拒绝，不评分。 |
| 多了或少了字段 | 照样评分。 | 拒绝，不评分。 |
| 没有名单 | 整段程序都可以改。 | 仍是整段程序。不走这层对照。 |

**输入例子**

整条流程不动。每一轮把一份 JSON 送进同一条流程。固定程序读这份 JSON，返回分数。

起点：

```json
{
  "pos_2": "T",
  "pos_4": "K",
  "model": "fixed"
}
```

这次允许改的字段：`pos_2`、`pos_4`。

合法候选。只改了 `pos_2`。这份会去评分：

```json
{
  "pos_2": "A",
  "pos_4": "K",
  "model": "fixed"
}
```

改了 `model`、多了字段、少了字段，或者把这份 JSON 换成一段程序，都不评分。确认界面上，这份 JSON 就是三行的表，用户勾选 `pos_2` 和 `pos_4`。

考虑过但未采用：给每一次本机候选沙箱放开网络和设备（隔离测试会失效，不可信代码也会拿到加速器）；把整个搜索放进那个不上网的沙箱（搜索要调用模型，档案也要留在 API 能读到的地方）；把“只能改这些字段”写成提示词（模型可以不遵守）；让候选自己报分；把某个具体模型或场景写进产品模块、单元测试或系统测试（那个场景不是这次改动）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增公共 HTTP API。域的缝不变：`evaluate(code, shards) -> (valid, metrics, error)`。NPU 路径复用本轮对话所选 Runner 上的现有 Shell 执行接口（`POST /shell-executions`、状态、日志、取消）。Runner 的选择和请求签名仍由 API 负责。这些接口若有调整，必须保持现有技能的启动行为不变，包括抗体流水线和 CodonTransformer。

新行为是现有引擎上的可选项：使用选中 Runner 的评分，以及用户勾选字段得到的可选 `direction`。运行前的确认显示字段表。本 issue 不新增针对某个模型的域、技能或夹具。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `services/evolve`：增加可选的 Runner 评分和方向检查。现有评分方式保持现在的行为。不改 `vendor/puct/search.py`，也不改默认的本机沙箱配置。
- `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py`：继续锁住本机隔离。若为了让普通候选看见网络或加速器而放宽这些测试，本 issue 不算完成。
- Evolve 的确认和运行面板：开始前的字段表，以及运行中的旧值、新值、分数。这个界面不直接显示原始 JSON。
- 技能执行：NPU 搜索使用和现有 NPU 技能相同的 Shell 执行约定，包括 Runner 上的沙箱和已经勾选的卡。不调用 `run_npu_job`。
- 不修改抗体技能和 MindSpore 算子。一次 NPU 作业完成不能证明 RFdiffusion、ProteinMPNN 或 Protenix 可用。
- 技能库发布、回放和外层循环不在范围内。本 issue 不得把内层结果写入技能库。

## 测试设计与测试计划

默认 CI 不需要昇腾设备。测试使用一个说 Shell 执行状态的 Runner 替身。测试不点名模型、不加载权重、不内置场景。单元测试和系统测试都不放替身模型。端到端用例如果以后确实要加，是另一次改动，不进入 `pnpm evolve:test`。

- **单元测试，NPU 作业。** `device=npu` 的完成记录返回 `valid=True`，分数来自固定程序返回的数字。候选自己打印的数字不记。排队、运行中、未知、产物缺失、设备不是 `npu`、失败或取消，都返回 `valid=False`，分数为空，不是 `0`。每个候选有自己的执行编号。单元测试不导入模型运行时。
- **单元测试，方向。** 未知字段被拒绝。不在 `direction.editable` 里的字段被改动时被拒绝。设置了方向时，自由形式的程序被拒绝。没有方向的 scorecard 不走这层检查。已经见过且没有提升的修改不成为新节点。失败重试到达上限后停止，并且不再另占搜索名额；等待不算重试。
- **单元测试，沙箱回归。** `tests/test_puct_sandbox.py` 保持原样：拒绝网络、写入限制在临时目录、没有隔离后端就拒绝运行、CPU 预算下限不变。构造 NPU 路径不会把默认的本机沙箱改成允许网络或设备。没有 Runner 的搜索不提交远程执行。
- **字段表。** 开始前，确认界面显示字段名、当前值，以及这次能不能改。运行中，一行显示改了哪一项、旧值、新值、分数。过长的值先显示开头，点开再看全文。
- **回归，也就是基线。** 现有 scorecard、PUCT 保真、script-domain、评审和测试门测试不改断言也要通过。这就是证明今天的 Evolve 仍和 `main` 上一样。抗体流水线测试不属于本 issue，不得为了变绿去改它们。
- **不放进单元测试或系统测试。** 不做某个模型的前向，不放场景技能或场景夹具。如果单独跑过硬件，单独报告，不算进 `pnpm evolve:test`。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm evolve:test`。未改过的 `main` 上原有用例的通过数和跳过数保持不变，再加上上面这些新测试。没有加速器的机器也必须能通过这条命令。

- [ ] 产品代码、单元测试和系统测试里没有替身模型、场景技能或场景夹具。以后的端到端用例不属于本 issue。
- [ ] `vendor/puct/search.py` 没有改动。`skills/` 下没有第二套搜索实现。
- [ ] `pnpm evolve:test` 通过。内层结果不发布到技能库。

## 补充信息

双层设计的最终科学验收仍是一次完整抗体设计，不是本 issue 的验收项。

813.author: HugoXK
813.body:
## What happened

On 2026-11-03 the model gateway started answering `503 Service is too busy` (`type: service_unavailable_error`, wrapped by the product as `[181001] model call failed … model_gateway_error`). Every queued pull request then failed L3 real E2E in the merge queue, and the queue drained nothing.

Three merge-queue runs from the same window, three different revisions, the same two jobs red (`L3 real E2E / Real E2E (basic)` and `L3 real E2E / Account for real cases`, then `merge-gate`):

| PR | merge_group run | merge queue head | L3 basic | Account |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #810 | [41614272116](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41614272116) | `b4379ac3` | failure | failure |
| #810 | [41613281893](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41613281893) | `03b27a13` | failure | failure |
| #715 | [41614268417](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41614268417) | `68ddebba` | failure | failure |
| #775 | [41614267932](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41614267932) | `f727b104` | failure | failure |

The verdict for #810's run [41614272116](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41614272116) (`real-e2e-verdict` artifact, `verdict.json`):

```
status FAIL, exitCode 1
planned 9, reported 9, executed 9
passed 1, failed 8, skipped 0
providerFaults 0, providerFaultRetries 0
problems: "basic: SHARD_FAILED", then 8 × "FAIL: <case key>"
```

So the gateway outage is reported as a **product failure**, not as a provider fault, and the retry path never engages. That contradicts the guarantee #548/#232 established: a provider fault is reported as `PROVIDER_FAULT: <case>` and never as `FAIL: <case>`.

## Why the fault is lost

The gateway text reaches the case as the assertion's own message. Both journeys do:

- `test/journey-basic-real-api.spec.ts:100` — `expect(terminal.status,terminal.error).toBe('completed');`
- `test/journey-runner-recovery-real.spec.ts:109` — same line

The second argument means one Playwright `error.message` carries **both** the gateway's 503 and the assertion block. From the L3 job log of run 41614268417:

```
Error: [181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: InternalServerError: Error code: 503 -
  {'error': {'message': 'Model request failed with status 503: {"error":{"message":"Service is too busy. ...",
  "type":"service_unavailable_error","code":"service_unavailable_error"}}', 'type': 'model_gateway_error'}}
expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality
Expected: "completed"
Received: "failed"
```

`detectProviderFault` (`test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs`) classifies the first half as a fault and then discards it because the same string matches `PRODUCT_REPORT` (`\bexpected\s*:|\breceived\s*:|\bassertion\b`) — the veto that protects a product failure which merely *quotes* a status also swallows a status the gateway itself produced. Reproduced by replaying the classifier on the two halves of that text:

```
gateway text alone          => {"code":"provider-server-error","status":503}
assertion block alone       => null
gateway text + assertion    => null      <-- the shape that actually occurs
```

`detectProviderFaultFromErrors` makes it worse for a case with several messages: it returns a fault only when **every** message classifies, so one assertion-only message vetoes a case that also carries the gateway's 503.

## Impact

- An outage is attributed to the pull request under review; in the queue it reads as a product regression for every candidate at once.
- `providerFaultRetries` stays 0, so the bounded early repeat that #548 added for exactly this situation never runs.
- No queued PR can merge while the provider is down (see the open question below, which is separate from the classification bug).

## Proposed fix

1. Let the gateway's own vocabulary win over the assertion wrapper: if `GATEWAY_CONTEXT` (`181001`, `model call failed`, `openai api`, `chat/completions`) and a 5xx status are present, classify as a provider fault even when `Expected:` / `Received:` appear. Keep `PRODUCT_REPORT` superior when the text quotes a status only — the existing `provider-fault.test.mjs` cases pin that direction and should stay green.
2. In `detectProviderFaultFromErrors`, treat the case as a fault when at least one message classifies and no message reports a product delivery miss, instead of requiring every message to classify.

This does not soften the gate floor from #548: a remaining provider fault still exits non-zero and still is not a pass. It only makes the failure named correctly, so the retry path can run and the queue can tell an outage from a regression.

## Open question (policy, not part of the fix)

#548 deliberately keeps `PROVIDER_FAULT` non-passing, so a full gateway outage still blocks the merge queue with no escape for any candidate. Should the merge-queue L3 profile get one bounded re-enqueue — or a neutral/skipped result — when the verdict is entirely provider faults? No proposal here beyond the question; the floor itself is not being reopened.

## Acceptance

- A case whose error message contains `[181001] model call failed … 503` **and** `Expected: "completed"` / `Received: "failed"` is counted as `PROVIDER_FAULT`, and the verdict reports `providerFaults > 0`.
- A product-only failure (a delivery miss with no gateway text) still counts as `FAIL` and still turns the verdict into `FAIL`.
- `node --test .ci/provider-fault.test.mjs` stays green, plus a new case for the mixed gateway-plus-assertion shape.

817.author: zhaochen39
817.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

The CI today is a cumulative gate model: PRs run L1/L2, the merge group runs L3, the nightly runs L4 and a release runs L5 (see the header comment of `.github/workflows/ci.yml`). As the suite grows, three engineering capabilities have to be built in step:

1. **Test coverage**: the Coverage job merges only the UT and ST layers, the mocked browser E2E is not measured, and no gate reads the published coverage as an admission threshold.
2. **CI stability**: real-model E2E (L3/L4/L5) depends on external services and credentials, and occasional failures have no systematic mechanism for flake identification, isolation and tracking.
3. **Release CI efficiency**: the L5 release pipeline has no end-to-end budget of <5 hours, and the bulk data downloads (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install, dependencies, datasets) happen again on every run.

Related files:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the L1–L5 pipeline: policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e jobs)
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml` (real E2E; `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs)
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` (the L5 release)
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs` (the case catalog and profile selection)
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`, `.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`, `.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs` (policy and result summaries)
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs` (coverage merge and summary)

## Design Ideas

### 1. Test coverage

**Baseline** — the `releases/v0.3.0.beta` line, authoritative run at `6d3c49a`:

| metric | whole repo | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| lines | 73.11% (105840/144777) | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| branches | 63.59% (39639/62335) | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| functions | 81.43% (7208/8852) | 81.43% | — |

- Weakest modules by line coverage: `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `scripts` 63.49%, `artifact-json` 63.16%, `specialist` 68.51%, `gateway` 68.40%.
- Cases: 3934 tagged — UT 3694/3806, ST 2/4, E2E 69/124; real-model 0/16, LLM judge 0/8, external 0/89, legacy 0/42.

**Gaps**

- Coverage is display-only: no gate reads it, and the `external` / `real` / `llm` classes are permanently 0.

**Plan**

1. Gate on industry health lines rather than the current 73%:

| metric | healthy | excellent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| lines | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| branches | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| functions (Node) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| statements | ≥80% | — |
| new / changed code (diff on a PR) | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| core paths (auth, sandbox execution, gateway, API routes) | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| per-package floor | ≥60% | — |

2. Land it in that order: diff coverage is enforced immediately (new code meets the line, existing code is not blocked), and the whole-repo figure ratchets upward and may never fall.

3. Starting gap: lines 73.11% (−6.89pt), branches 63.59% (−6.41pt), functions 81.43% (already passing). Four packages sit below the 60% floor — `idea-tree` 45.61%, `schema` 51.84%, `web` 56.14%, `services/runner` 0% — and each gets its own raise target.

4. Case-level coverage, not just a case count: a profile is the gate tier a run resolves to (`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`), and `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` states which tag combinations each one selects. Today the 16 real-model, 8 LLM-judge and 89 external cases are selected by no profile at all, so they never run and read 0 forever; every case must either be selected by a profile or explicitly marked out of scope in the tag catalog, so the omission surfaces at review time.

5. Tie cases to modules: the tagged catalog carries the case-to-module mapping, so a new module without an executing case fails the gate, and `planned / executed / passed` remains the execution view beside it.

**Cases no profile can ever select.** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` defines every profile as one of five rules (L1/L2 hermetic, L3/L4/L5 real), so a tag combination outside those rules never runs. On the `main` catalog (359 cases), 45 are permanently dead:

| tag shape | why no rule matches | cases |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status:legacy` | hermetic accepts only `reviewed`; real only `reviewed` / `external` | 42 |
| `status:quarantined` | same, with no path back in | 1 |
| `category:st` + `model:real` | the real rule is pinned to `category:e2e` | 1 |
| `npu:required` | all five rules require `npu:none` | 1 |

Four more shapes are structurally dead and simply have no case yet: `os:macos` / `os:windows`, `arch:arm64` outside real e2e, `judge:llm` combined with `model:none` / `mock`, and any case missing a `tier` tag — the old release-line catalog has no tier dimension, so under today's policy it would match nothing at all.

A further 131 cases read 0 without being dead: 61 UT and 70 real e2e do run, but the `ut` and `e2e-real` slice catalogs are never uploaded (`slices` registers only `e2e` and `st`), so their execution cannot be attributed.

- Fix the 45: delete or migrate the 42 `legacy` cases, give `quarantined` an exit, retag `st` + `real` as `e2e` or mark it out of scope, and open a separate NPU tier or declare it unsupported.
- Reachability check in the catalog check (`ci:catalog:check`, reusing the rule union exported by `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs`): a case whose tags match no profile fails catalog generation, so a dead case is caught at review time instead of reading 0 for months.

### 2. CI stability

- Automatic failure classification: product defect / environment / external dependency / test flake.
- Flake governance: when a case's failure rate over its last N runs crosses a threshold, mark it quarantined automatically — it keeps running and recording results, but its failure no longer blocks merges, and a tracking issue is opened for the owner. It leaves quarantine once it passes N consecutive runs, so a flaky case neither freezes the queue nor silently disappears.
- No blanket retry. A case is rerun only when its failure is attributable to network jitter or an unstable gateway / upstream — connect and read timeouts, connection resets, DNS failures, HTTP 429/5xx, interrupted streams. Every other failure, including a flaky real-model case, is reported as it happened and handled by the classification and quarantine above. A retry is labelled as an infrastructure retry, its count is visible per case, and sustained gateway failures beyond the retry budget are reported as an infrastructure incident rather than a test failure.
- Explore disabling the model's thinking mode, or setting the reasoning effort to its lowest level: much of the flakiness of the real-model cases comes from the randomness of the reasoning path; disabling or minimizing thinking narrows the output variance, makes the results more reproducible, and shortens per-case inference time (an efficiency win as well). The conclusion has to be backed by an A/B experiment — run both configurations N times each, compare pass rates and failure variance; if the pass rate does not regress beyond the accepted bound, fix it as a CI-only inference configuration applied to the L3/L4/L5 journeys only, leaving the product default untouched.

### 3. Release CI efficiency (<5h)

- Give the L5 pipeline a 5-hour end-to-end budget, add a timing view of actual per-job duration against that budget, and alert automatically when it is exceeded.
- Compress duration through caching (pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm are cached already), parallel test sharding (the mocked E2E matrix exists; extend it to UT/ST), and trimming redundant layers from the release profile.
- Run the real-model journeys at the lowest thinking effort: thinking off, or reasoning effort at its minimum, for L3/L4/L5 — reasoning tokens are the dominant cost of a case, so this shortens per-case latency directly. It is the same A/B switch as the stability item; here it is measured as p50/p95 duration per case against the 5-hour budget and fixed once the pass rate shows no regression.
- Data-download optimization: inventory the bulk downloads in the pipeline (the ~1.5 GB JiuwenSwarm install with its virtualenv, pnpm / uv dependencies, test datasets and fixtures, model and sidecar data, Docker images, and the base images of the release binaries) and eliminate the repeated ones item by item — pre-download into `actions/cache`, use an internal mirror / CDN, prefetch in parallel with the build steps, and key the cache on lockfiles / content hashes. Track download time separately in the budget view; a rerun with a cache hit must not download the bulk again.
- Produce an L5 duration baseline report marking the top-N slowest jobs and the optimization suggestions (including the share of download time).

## Involved Public APIs

No new or changed product public APIs; all of this is CI-internal capability.

- Reuse the existing CI-internal interfaces: `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...` (case selection), the `.ci-results` directory layout, and the `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` inputs of `real-e2e.yml`.
- The new outputs (coverage report and duration baseline report) are uploaded as artifacts, following the existing artifact naming convention (e.g. `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`).

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `.ci/` scripts: the policy, matrix and summary scripts are extended to emit coverage and timing data.
- `test/support/tagged`: the case catalog gains coverage-ownership and flake-marker fields.
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`, `scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`: a wider merge scope and a new output format.
- `release.yml`: the L5 budget check hooks into the existing `workflow_call` chain.
- No product code changes (apps/*, services/*); the model thinking-mode configuration is injected through the CI / E2E harness only and does not touch product defaults.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Coverage**: with a change of a known coverage delta, verify that the PR comment and the threshold block trigger correctly; verify the numbers are sound once the E2E layer is included.
- **Stability**: on a test branch, produce deterministic failures and random failures, and verify the classification, the quarantine isolation and the auto-issue flow; inject network jitter and gateway failures (timeout, connection reset, 429/5xx, interrupted stream) and verify the case is retried and, when it then passes, recorded as a pass with a visible retry count, while a product-defect failure is not retried; run the thinking-mode A/B experiment N times per arm, and verify that the failure variance narrows with no unacceptable pass-rate regression.
- **Efficiency**: take the last 3 release runs as the baseline, verify that the budget view times correctly and that the L5 end-to-end is <5 hours after the optimization; verify that the bulk data downloads take near-zero time on a cache hit; and record the per-case p50/p95 duration with thinking off or at its lowest, before and after.
- All of the above is CI behavior and automatable within L2; no new real-model cases are added (the existing L4/L5 journeys are reused).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Coverage is gated on the industry health lines: whole-repo lines ≥80%, branches ≥70%, functions ≥80% and statements ≥80%; new code ≥80% diff coverage; each package ≥60% and core paths ≥90%.
- [ ] Case-level coverage is closed: no case sits outside every profile, and every module maps to at least one case the gating profile actually executes.
- [ ] Flaky cases are identified and quarantined automatically; only failures caused by network jitter or an unstable gateway are retried, labelled as infrastructure retries and never applied to product defects; the thinking-mode (off / lowest) A/B experiment is concluded and, if viable, fixed as a CI-only inference configuration.
- [ ] The L5 release CI finishes end-to-end in <5 hours with in-pipeline over-budget alerts, every bulk download is cache/prefetch managed with no re-download on a cache hit, and the real-model journeys run at the lowest thinking effort with the latency gain recorded.

## Additional Information

- This is an engineering-effectiveness request; maintainers are invited to schedule it as the three sub-items above.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

当前 CI 采用累积门禁模型：PR 跑 L1/L2，merge_group 跑 L3，nightly 跑 L4，发布跑 L5（见 `.github/workflows/ci.yml` 头部注释）。随着用例规模增长，三个方面的工程能力需要同步建设：

1. **用例覆盖度**：Coverage 任务只合并 UT、ST 两层，mocked browser E2E 未被度量，且没有任何门禁把已发布的覆盖度作为准入阈值。
2. **CI 稳定性**：真实模型 E2E（L3/L4/L5）依赖外部服务与凭据，偶发失败缺乏系统性的抖动识别、隔离与跟踪机制。
3. **版本 CI 效率**：L5 发布流水线尚无 <5 小时的端到端时长预算约束，大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB、依赖、数据集）在每次运行中反复发生。

相关文件：

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`（L1–L5 主流水线：policy / ut / st / coverage / e2e-plan / real-e2e 等 job）
- `.github/workflows/real-e2e.yml`（真实 E2E；`profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入）
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`（L5 发布）
- `test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`（用例目录与 profile 选择）
- `.ci/tier-policy.mjs`、`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`、`.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`（策略与结果汇总）
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`（覆盖度合并与摘要）

## 设计思路

### 1. 用例覆盖度

**基线**——取 `releases/v0.3.0.beta` 线（authoritative，SHA `6d3c49a`）：

| 指标 | 整仓 | Node | Python |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 行 | 73.11%（105840/144777） | 73.19% | 72.08% |
| 分支 | 63.59%（39639/62335） | 63.85% | 59.63% |
| 函数 | 81.43%（7208/8852） | 81.43% | — |

- 行覆盖率最弱的模块：`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`scripts` 63.49%、`artifact-json` 63.16%、`specialist` 68.51%、`gateway` 68.40%。
- 用例：3934 个，UT 覆盖 3694/3806、ST 2/4、E2E 69/124；真实模型 0/16、LLM judge 0/8、external 0/89、legacy 0/42。

**问题**

- 覆盖度只用于展示，没有任何门禁读取；`external` / `real` / `llm` 三类用例恒为 0。

**方案**

1. 门禁取业界健康线，而不是当前的 73%：

| 指标 | 健康线 | 优秀线 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 行覆盖 | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 分支覆盖 | ≥70% | ≥85% |
| 函数覆盖（Node） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 语句覆盖 | ≥80% | — |
| 新增/变更代码（PR diff） | ≥80% | ≥90% |
| 核心链路（认证、沙箱执行、网关、API 路由） | ≥90% | ≥95% |
| 单包下限 | ≥60% | — |

2. 按上述顺序落地：diff 覆盖立即生效（新代码按健康线走，不阻塞存量），整仓数值以棘轮方式只升不降。

3. 当前差距：行 73.11%（差 6.89pt）、分支 63.59%（差 6.41pt）、函数 81.43%（已达标）。4 个包低于 60% 下限——`idea-tree` 45.61%、`schema` 51.84%、`web` 56.14%、`services/runner` 0%——各自设定提升目标。

4. 用例维度覆盖，而不只是用例数量：profile 是一次运行解析出的门禁档位（`pr` / `merge` / `daily` / `release`），具体选中哪些 tag 组合由 `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 定义。目前 16 个真实模型、8 个 LLM judge、89 个 external 用例不被任何 profile 选中，等于永远不跑、永远显示 0；要求每条用例要么被某个 profile 选中，要么在 tag 目录中显式标注「不在范围」，让遗漏在评审阶段就暴露。

5. 用例与模块绑定：tag 目录维护「用例 → 模块」映射，新增模块若没有可执行用例则门禁失败；`planned / executed / passed` 作为与之并列的执行视图。

**永远不会被任何 profile 选中的用例。** `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 把每个 profile 定义为五条规则之一（L1/L2 hermetic、L3/L4/L5 real），不符合这些规则的 tag 组合永远不会被执行。以 `main` 目录（359 条）为例，45 条是彻底死用例：

| tag 形态 | 为何无规则命中 | 条数 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `status:legacy` | hermetic 只收 `reviewed`，real 只收 `reviewed` / `external` | 42 |
| `status:quarantined` | 同上，且没有回到门禁的路径 | 1 |
| `category:st` + `model:real` | real 规则硬编码 `category:e2e` | 1 |
| `npu:required` | 五条规则全部要求 `npu:none` | 1 |

另有四类结构性死角，目前恰好没有对应用例：`os:macos` / `os:windows`、非 real e2e 的 `arch:arm64`、`judge:llm` 搭配 `model:none` / `mock`，以及任何缺少 `tier` 标签的用例——release 线那份旧目录没有 tier 维度，按当前策略会全部失配。

还有 131 条显示为 0 但并不属于死用例：61 条 UT 与 70 条 real e2e 实际在跑，只是 `ut` 与 `e2e-real` 两个切片的 catalog 从未上传（`slices` 只登记了 `e2e` 和 `st`），导致执行结果无法归因。

- 处置 45 条：删除或迁移 42 条 `legacy`；为 `quarantined` 补上出口；`st` + `real` 改 tag 为 `e2e` 或标注不在范围；`npu` 单独开档位或声明不支持。
- 在 catalog 校验（`ci:catalog:check`，复用 `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` 导出的规则并集）中增加可达性检查：用例 tag 若不属于任何 profile，catalog 生成即失败，让死用例在评审阶段暴露，而不是显示 0 数月。

### 2. CI 稳定性提升

- 失败自动归类：产品缺陷 / 环境 / 外部依赖 / 用例抖动（flake）。
- 抖动治理（quarantine）：同一用例近 N 次运行失败率超阈值时自动标记为隔离——它继续运行并记录结果，但失败不再阻断合并，同时自动创建跟踪 issue 派给 owner；连续 N 次通过后自动解除隔离，既不冻结合并队列，也不会让用例悄悄消失。
- 不做统一重试。仅当失败可归因于网络抖动或网关、上游不稳定（连接与读取超时、连接重置、DNS 失败、HTTP 429/5xx、流中断）时才自动重跑；其他失败——包括真实模型用例本身的抖动——如实上报，交由上面的失败归类与 quarantine 处理。重试会标注为基础设施重试，用例维度可看到次数，超出重试预算的持续性网关失败按基础设施故障上报，而不是记为用例失败。
- 探索关闭或调低模型思考模式（thinking / reasoning effort 设为最低档）：真实模型用例的抖动很大程度来自推理路径的随机性，关闭/调低思考模式可收窄输出方差、提升可复现性，同时缩短单用例推理耗时（兼具效率收益）。结论需以 A/B 实验数据支撑：对比开启 vs 关闭（或最低档）两组各 N 次运行的通过率与失败方差，若通过率无可接受退化，则固化为 CI 专用推理配置，仅作用于 L3/L4/L5 journey，不影响产品默认行为。

### 3. 版本 CI 效率提升（<5hr）

- 为 L5 流水线定义端到端时长预算 5 小时，pipeline 内增加各 job 实际耗时 vs 预算的计时看板，超预算自动告警。
- 通过缓存（pnpm / uv / JiuwenSwarm 已有）、用例分片并行（mocked E2E matrix 已具备，推广到 UT/ST）、release profile 裁剪冗余层级来压缩时长。
- 真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行：L3/L4/L5 关闭思考或把 reasoning effort 调到最低——推理 token 是单个用例的主要开销，这一步直接缩短单用例耗时。与稳定性项共用同一组 A/B 开关，这里以每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对照 5 小时预算衡量，确认通过率无退化后固化。
- 数据下载优化：盘点流水线中的大额数据下载（JiuwenSwarm 安装约 1.5 GB 及其 virtualenv、pnpm / uv 依赖、测试数据集与 fixture、模型与 sidecar 数据、Docker 镜像、二进制基础镜像），逐项消除重复下载——预下载进 `actions/cache`、走内部镜像源 / CDN、与构建步骤并行预取、按 lockfile / 内容寻址命中缓存；下载耗时单独计时并纳入预算看板，缓存命中后的重复运行不应再产生大额下载。
- 输出 L5 耗时基线报告，标注 top-N 耗时 job 与优化建议（含下载耗时占比）。

## 涉及的公共 API

不新增、不修改产品公共 API；全部为 CI 内部能力。

- 复用现有 CI 内部接口：`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs list --profile ... --slice ...`（用例选择）、`.ci-results` 结果目录格式、`real-e2e.yml` 的 `profile` / `backend` / `max-parallel` 输入。
- 新增产物（覆盖度报告、耗时基线报告）统一作为 artifacts 上传，遵循现有 artifact 命名约定（如 `node-coverage-summary-${scope}-${sha}`）。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `.ci/` 脚本：策略、矩阵、汇总脚本需扩展以输出覆盖度与耗时数据。
- `test/support/tagged`：用例目录需补充覆盖度归属与抖动标记字段。
- `scripts/coverage-report.mjs`、`scripts/coverage-job-summary.mjs`：扩展合并范围与输出格式。
- `release.yml`：L5 预算检查嵌入现有 `workflow_call` 链。
- 不改动产品代码（apps/*、services/*）；模型思考模式配置仅通过 CI / E2E harness 注入，不影响产品默认行为。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **覆盖度**：构造已知覆盖变化的变更，验证 PR 评论与阈值拦截正确触发；验证 E2E 层纳入后报告数值合理。
- **稳定性**：在测试分支制造确定性失败与随机失败，验证分类、quarantine 隔离与自动建单流程；注入网络抖动与网关失败（超时、连接重置、429/5xx、流中断），验证用例被自动重试、重试后通过则记为通过且重试次数可见，而产品缺陷类失败不触发重试；思考模式 A/B 实验两组各跑 N 次，验证关闭/最低档下失败方差收窄且通过率无可接受退化。
- **效率**：以最近 3 次 release 运行作为基线，验证预算看板计时准确，优化后 L5 端到端 <5 小时；验证缓存命中后大额数据下载耗时趋近于零；记录关闭/最低思考强度前后每条用例的 p50/p95 耗时对比。
- 上述验证均为 CI 自身行为，属于 L2 可自动化校验范围；不新增真实模型用例（复用现有 L4/L5 journey）。

## 验收标准

- [ ] 覆盖度按业界健康线设门禁：整仓行 ≥80%、分支 ≥70%、函数 ≥80%、语句 ≥80%；新代码 diff 覆盖 ≥80%；单包 ≥60%、核心链路 ≥90%。
- [ ] 用例维度覆盖闭环：没有用例落在所有 profile 之外，每个模块都至少映射到一个门禁 profile 实际执行的用例。
- [ ] CI 具备抖动用例自动识别与 quarantine 机制；仅网络抖动 / 网关不稳定导致的失败自动重试，标注为基础设施重试且不适用于产品缺陷；完成模型思考模式（关闭/最低档）A/B 实验并形成结论，可行则固化为 CI 专用推理配置。
- [ ] L5 版本 CI 端到端时长 <5 小时，流水线内有超预算告警；大额数据下载全部纳入缓存/预下载管理，缓存命中后无冗余下载；真实模型用例以最低思考强度运行并记录耗时收益。

## 补充信息

- 本 issue 为工程效能类需求，建议 maintainer 按三个子项拆分任务排期。

# [Bug] /health serially awaits downstream services beyond Docker HEALTHCHECK timeout budget

## Summary

The API service's `/health` (and `/api/health`) endpoint awaits two downstream health checks **in series**: the Runner and the Memory Graph sidecar. The Runner check is bounded by an explicit 5-second `AbortSignal.timeout`, but the Memory Graph check has **no application-level timeout** in the fetch call. Docker's `HEALTHCHECK` for the API container is configured with a 5-second timeout. Under degraded downstream conditions the serial composition can therefore exceed the Docker budget, and the container can be reported `unhealthy` even though the API process itself is still live.

This issue is about the **design of the health probe composition**. It is not about the security exposure of `/health` (tracked separately in #267).

## Source locations

| Component | File | Line(s) | Observation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `/health` route (serial composition) | `services/api/src/http/index.ts` | 793–821 | Two sequential `await` calls |
| Runner health check (bounded) | `packages/executor/src/runner-client.ts` | 161–169 | `AbortSignal.timeout(5_000)` |
| Memory Graph health check (unbounded) | `packages/memory/src/memory-graph.ts` | ~344 | `fetch(this.baseUrl + "/health")` with no `signal` |
| Docker HEALTHCHECK | `Dockerfile` | ~275–276 | `--interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=60s --retries=5` |

Relevant excerpts:

```typescript
// services/api/src/http/index.ts:793-821
if (request.method === "GET" && (url.pathname === "/health" || url.pathname === "/api/health")) {
  const runner = await runnerClient.health().catch(() => undefined);
  const memoryGraph = store.getMemoryGraphSettings().enabled
    ? await memoryGraphClient.health().catch(() => "degraded")
    : "disabled";
  // ... build response ...
  sendJson(response, 200, { ... });
  return;
}
```

```typescript
// packages/executor/src/runner-client.ts:161-169
async health(): Promise<RunnerHealth> {
  const sentAt = Date.now();
  const response = await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}/health`, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5_000) });
  // ...
}
```

```typescript
// packages/memory/src/memory-graph.ts (~line 344)
async health(): Promise<string> {
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${this.baseUrl}/health`); // no AbortSignal
    if (!response.ok) { /* ... */ return "degraded"; }
    // ...
  } catch { /* ... */ return "degraded"; }
}
```

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile (~line 275)
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=60s --retries=5 \
  CMD curl --silent --fail http://127.0.0.1:4310/health || exit 1
```

## Expected behavior

- The liveness probe should reflect the API process's own ability to respond within the Docker `HEALTHCHECK` timeout.
- Each downstream check should be individually bounded so that the sum of their latencies cannot exceed the probe budget.
- A slow or unresponsive downstream should report `degraded` for that component, not stall the entire `/health` response.

## Actual behavior

- The two downstream checks run in series. The total latency is `latency(runner) + latency(memoryGraph)`.
- The Runner check is bounded at 5 s.
- The Memory Graph check has **no explicit application-level timeout**. Its effective upper bound is whatever the underlying TCP / socket layer decides (connection timeout, TLS handshake, server-side idle), which is environment-dependent and not controlled by the API process.
- The Docker `HEALTHCHECK` budget is 5 s, with `--retries=5` before the container is marked `unhealthy`.

Under normal conditions the composed latency is well below 5 s. Under degraded downstream conditions (cold-starting sidecar, Neo4j under load, bind-mount I/O pressure, network congestion) the Memory Graph leg can stretch, and the composed latency can exceed the Docker budget.

## Observed correlation (not a causation claim)

In one local Windows + Docker Desktop run the Docker health history reported `FailingStreak = 18` for the API container. The serial-composition design above is a **plausible contributing factor**, but this issue does **not** claim to have proven that the Memory Graph leg was the root cause of those specific failures. Other contributors (sidecar startup ordering, Neo4j readiness, host I/O scheduling) may also be involved. The observation is recorded because it motivated the investigation; it is not offered as evidence of a specific failure mechanism.

## Risk

- **False-negative liveness**: Docker marks the API container `unhealthy` while the API process is still capable of serving requests.
- **Orchestration side effects**: depending on the deployment's `restart` policy, an `unhealthy` container may be restarted, interrupted, or removed from a load balancer — none of which are appropriate responses to a slow downstream.
- **User-visible impact**: the web client reads `/health` to populate the Memory Graph status indicator; a stalled `/health` can cause the UI to flicker between `ok` / `degraded` / `unavailable`.
- **Composable design debt**: as more downstream services are added to `/health`, the serial composition will make the probe increasingly fragile.

## Reproduction

1. Start the SD stack (`scripts/start-stack.sh` or `docker compose up`).
2. Confirm the Memory Graph sidecar is enabled in System Settings.
3. Introduce a delay on the Memory Graph's `/health` path. Two practical ways:
   - Pause the Neo4j container (`docker pause <neo4j>`), or
   - Use a traffic-shaping tool (e.g. `tc netem`) on the sidecar's network namespace to add ≥ 4 s latency.
4. In a loop, measure the API's `/health` response time:
   ```bash
   while true; do
     curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{time_total}\n" http://127.0.0.1:4310/health
     sleep 2
   done
   ```
5. Observe that the measured latency grows to match the injected delay, and that once it exceeds 5 s Docker's `HEALTHCHECK` begins to fail.
6. After `--retries=5` consecutive failures, `docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' <api-container>` reports `unhealthy`.

## Suggested directions (for upstream consideration, not prescriptive)

- **Bound the Memory Graph check**: add an `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` to the fetch call in `memory-graph.ts` so the probe is self-bounded.
- **Split liveness from readiness**: keep `/health` minimal (API process only) for Docker, and expose a separate `/ready` that composes downstream status for the UI and orchestrator.
- **Parallelize downstream checks**: if composition is kept, run the two checks with `Promise.all` so the composed latency is the max rather than the sum.
- **Make the Docker budget authoritative**: ensure the composed worst-case latency is strictly less than `HEALTHCHECK --timeout`, with headroom for OS scheduling.

## Environment where this was observed

- OS: Windows 11 (22631)
- Runtime: Docker Desktop with bind-mounted data directory (9P filesystem)
- SD build: `sd-catalystpi-probe` worktree, M4 milestone
- Memory Graph backend: Neo4j sidecar

## Relates to

- #267 — `/health` security exposure (orthogonal; this issue is about latency budget, not authentication).
818.title: [Bug] /health serially awaits downstream services beyond Docker HEALTHCHECK timeout budget

# [Bug] Agent run stalls after todo_create tool.started without completion event and hits 240s idle timeout

## Summary

During a real end-to-end run on the SD stack, the agent's event stream stopped emitting progress for roughly **4 minutes 13 seconds** immediately after a `tool.started` event for the `todo_create` tool. No matching `tool.output` or `tool.completed` event was ever emitted for that invocation. The run was then terminated by the gateway's idle-timeout watchdog with the error:

```
Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms
```

This issue records the **observed fault symptom** and the associated evidence. The **internal root cause is not determined**: we do not know whether the stall happened inside the `todo_create` tool implementation, the gateway's tool-dispatch layer, the model gateway, or an underlying runtime component. Attribution to any specific component (SiliconFlow, SQLite, network, single gateway module, etc.) is intentionally **not** made here.

## Run identifiers

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Run ID | `a990cea3-bbf3-4e02-a0da-a4bd95237e79` |
| Session ID | `b52f69ac-eb99-4777-91ca-9aee2eb9063c` |
| Agent Run ID (evidence) | `9b87d4ab-0798-470b-bbb6-ed2c32167a65` |
| User Message ID | `ce4e1c3e-4f3b-495a-91f5-6285317c8664` |
| Model ID | `e1c88640-84b2-447c-ab9a-ef1e4604126b` |
| Skill selection mode | `all` (17 skills enabled) |
| Created at | `2026-11-03T11:14:19.514Z` |
| Started at | `2026-11-03T11:14:38.558Z` |
| Finished at | `2026-11-03T11:21:05.622Z` |
| Final status | `failed` |
| Terminal error | `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms` |

## Observed event sequence (stall window)

The SSE stream against `/api/sessions/{sid}/messages` (with `Accept: text/event-stream`) delivered the following frames around the stall window. All timestamps are UTC on 2026-11-03. `id` is the SSE sequence id; `receivedAt` is the client-side receive timestamp.

| SSE id | receivedAt | type | detail | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 149 | 11:16:27.313 | `agent.record` | `model.completed` (turn 1) | last model-completed record before tool call |
| 150 | 11:16:27.394 | `assistant.response.settled` | turn 2 | LLM response stream closed |
| **151** | **11:16:27.402** | **`tool.started`** | **`todo_create` (status `running`)** | **last normal progress event** |
| — | *11:16:27.402 – 11:20:40.144* | — | **no SSE frames received** | **~4 min 13 s stall window** |
| **152** | **11:20:40.144** | **`agent.record`** | **`state.committed`** | first event after stall window |
| **153** | **11:21:05.507** | **`run.failed`** | `error: "Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms"`, `errorCode: timeout` | terminal failure |
| 154 | 11:21:05.712 | `run.status` | `status: failed` | final state notification |

### What is missing

For every observed `tool.started` earlier in the same run, the stream delivered a matching `tool.output` (sometimes with a `null` SSE id) and a `tool.completed` within seconds:

| Tool | tool.started id | tool.output | tool.completed id |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rename_session` | 98 | line 99 (null id) | 99 |
| `list_files` | 100 | line 102 (null id) | 101 |
| **`todo_create`** | **151** | **— missing —** | **— missing —** |

The `todo_create` invocation is the only tool call in this run whose lifecycle is not closed.

## Evidence

- **Raw SSE capture**: `raw_sse.jsonl` (156 lines, covering SSE ids 1–154 plus two `tool.output` frames with null ids). The stall-window excerpt above is taken verbatim from this file.
- **Run final status**: `run_final_status.json` reports `status: failed`, `error: "Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms"`, `finishedAt: 2026-11-03T11:21:05.622Z`.
- **Idle-timeout source**: `services/api/src/agent-run/run-deadlines.ts` implements a dual deadline (turn + idle). The idle deadline is rearmed by `progress()` on every gateway event; if no progress is reported for `idleMs` (240 000 ms in this run), `expire("idle")` fires and the run is failed with the message observed above.
- **Progress trigger sites**: `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts` calls `markProgress()` from the SSE `emit()` path, the model-gateway progress path, the `run_started` path, and adapter events. During the stall window, none of these sites fired, consistent with the SSE stream going silent.

## Expected behavior

- A `tool.started` event should be followed by a `tool.output` and a `tool.completed` (or a `tool.failed`) within a bounded, reasonable interval.
- If a tool invocation cannot complete, the gateway should either time it out at a tool-level budget or surface a `tool.failed` event, so the run can terminate cleanly with an attributable cause.
- The idle watchdog should fire only when the gateway as a whole has truly stopped making progress, not as the primary symptom of a single tool hanging.

## Actual behavior

- After `tool.started(todo_create)` at 11:16:27.402Z, no further progress event was emitted for 4 min 13 s.
- No `tool.output` or `tool.completed` for `todo_create` was ever emitted.
- The idle watchdog fired at the 240 s budget and terminated the run with a generic stall error.
- The first post-stall event (`agent.record state.committed`) arrived 13 s after the inferred watchdog expiry; the terminal `run.failed` arrived 25 s after that.

## Impact

- The run's scientific work in progress (turn 1 of a multi-turn research plan) was lost.
- The user-visible error message (`no gateway progress for 240000 ms`) does not identify which component stalled, which makes self-diagnosis difficult.
- The missing tool lifecycle events make post-mortem attribution impossible from the SSE stream alone.

## Reproduction

1. Start the SD stack (`scripts/start-stack.sh` or `docker compose up`) on any host.
2. Create a project and a session.
3. Enable the default skill set (17 skills, including the one that exposes `todo_create`).
4. Send the following prompt (the same prompt used in the affected run):

   > 我正在研究 Pd 催化 1,3-二烯的选择性发散反应，希望理解不同配体、溶剂和 CO 条件如何影响羰基化与分子内环化路径。请识别关键科学问题、已知信息和未知信息，制定可执行的研究计划，并说明哪些步骤需要文献、计算或实验支持。不要直接给出未经验证的机理结论。

5. Open an SSE connection to `/api/sessions/{sid}/messages` with `Accept: text/event-stream`.
6. Observe whether a `tool.started` for `todo_create` is followed by matching `tool.output` / `tool.completed` events, or whether the stream stalls for minutes and ends with `run.failed` / `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms`.

The fault is **intermittent** in our experience: the same stack and prompt do not reproduce the stall on every run. That is part of what makes the issue worth tracking upstream — the manifestation is real, the trigger is not yet isolated.

## Environment where this was observed

- OS: Windows 11 (22631)
- Runtime: Docker Desktop with bind-mounted data directory (9P filesystem)
- SD build: `sd-catalystpi-probe` worktree, M4 milestone
- Model gateway: SiliconFlow (external LLM provider, via the SD model-gateway layer)
- Memory Graph backend: Neo4j sidecar

## What this issue is NOT claiming

- It does **not** attribute the stall to SiliconFlow, the model gateway, SQLite, the memory-graph sidecar, the network, or any single gateway component.
- It does **not** claim that the idle watchdog is wrong to fire; the watchdog behaved as designed. The question is why no progress was reported for 240 s.
- It does **not** claim that the stall is deterministically reproducible from the prompt alone.

## Suggested investigations (for upstream, not prescriptive)

- Add tool-lifecycle logging on the gateway: for every `tool.started`, record the matching `tool.output` / `tool.completed` / `tool.failed` and the elapsed time, even when the run is later terminated by the idle watchdog.
- Add a per-tool execution budget, independent of the run-level idle timeout, so a single hanging tool fails the tool rather than the whole run.
- Surface the stalled tool's name in the terminal `run.failed` error message, so users and operators can attribute the fault without replaying the SSE stream.
- Correlate this run's gateway-side logs (model-gateway requests, tool dispatch, adapter events) with the SSE capture to identify where the `todo_create` invocation stopped making progress.

## Relates to

- Issue A (same submission batch) — `/health` serial-composition design. Orthogonal; the two issues share the same local test environment but do not share a causal link.
819.title: [Bug] Agent run stalls after todo_create tool.started without completion event and hits 240s idle timeout

820.body:
### 🚀 Background Description

Some settings can already be changed in the chat. The agent can pick a registered model, change thinking settings, choose a skill or a library, enable a connector that is ready, and change this session's review preference. Every other setting still sends the user to the settings page.

This issue brings the remaining ordinary settings onto that same path. The agent proposes a change. The card shows the current value, the new value, and where it will apply: the deployment, a shared resource, the project, or the session. The user checks the card and confirms in the chat. A later task uses the saved value.

### Design Ideas

Reuse the configuration service and the confirmation card that already exist. The agent reads the current value, where that value is inherited from, and the choices that are allowed, then proposes only those fields.

The settings this path must cover:

1. Package sources and runners. Choose an existing pip or conda preset. Assign a registered runner to a project or a session, or turn that assignment off.
2. Proxy. Manage the shared proxy. Choose the proxy a model provider uses, and the proxy MCP uses. Changing the deployment's default route is confirmed on its own.
3. Web search and credentials. Change search, fetch, and cache within what Native and JiuwenSwarm already support. Replace or clear the key of a supported provider through the secure input.
4. Review, exploration tree, JSON preview, and inheritance. Choose whether the reviewer takes part. Pick a registered exploration-tree template and a supported strength and budget. Turn the dedicated JSON preview on or off. A limited set of ordinary project and session settings can go back to being inherited.
5. Safety and approval. Change the sandbox network, this session's approval, the default approval for a new session, and the low-risk auto-save policy. Each of these is confirmed on its own.
6. Models and providers. Edit the metadata and API identity of a model that already exists, and edit a shared provider connection together with its credential. Before saving, check the real address that will receive the credential.
7. Memory and Neo4j. Turn the workbench memory graph on or off. Choose local or Neo4j. Set the address and the user name. Replace or clear the Neo4j password on its own.
8. MCP servers that are already registered. Edit the metadata, timeout, enabled state, and supported overrides. Replace an existing credential header through the secure input. Deleting a custom server is confirmed on its own.

A permission or a safety policy is never folded into an ordinary confirmation. A secret is typed only into the secure input. The proposal, the preview, and the receipt show no secret.

These stay on the settings page for this issue: creating an MCP server, changing an MCP URL, OAuth, arbitrary headers or environment variables, import, and install. Registering a runner or SSH, creating an environment, and installing or removing packages. Plugin-only settings. The global reviewer-specialist switch. Free prompt text, scoring weights, and round counts inside an exploration-tree template.

### Involved Public APIs

Extend the conversational configuration API that already exists: which capabilities it can propose, which fields a proposal carries, and which confirmation a change requires. Discovery, preview, and save stay the same mechanisms. Each setting keeps its own scope, its own checks, and its own place for credentials. A caller that draws the card follows the capability and the confirmation the response returns.

### Description of Relevance to Other Modules

The settings list, the card, and the request service are shared by every area above. The result has to hold for Native and for JiuwenSwarm, for a project value and a session value that inherits it, and for a queued task that already took a snapshot of its configuration. Proxy choices and safety policy change how web search, model calls, MCP, and the sandbox reach the network. When a save must reconnect an external service or restart a process, that step is part of accepting the change.

### Test Design and Test Plan

Start the real application. With a real model, use the browser chat to propose a change in each area above, confirm it, save it, refresh, and read the value back. Run a later task and see that it uses the new value. Where a restart or a reconnect is required, include that step.

Refuse a permission change, a credential change, a proxy change, and an external connection. The secret must be absent from the chat, the preview, and the receipt.

Record the code version, the environment, and the result. After the areas land together, the shared settings list, the card, and the request service still answer as they do now.

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each setting listed above can be proposed in the chat. The card shows the current value, the new value, and where it applies.
- [ ] A permission, a safety policy, a credential destination, and deleting a custom server each wait for their own confirmation.
- [ ] A secret is entered only in the secure input and does not appear in the chat, the preview, or the receipt.
- [ ] After save and refresh, the value reads back, and a later task uses it.
- [ ] Settings named as out of scope above are unchanged.
- [ ] The check record names the code version, the environment, and the result.

### Additional Information

Package sources and runners are already in `main` (#727). The other areas are in #734, #737, #756, #758, #763, #770, and #773. This issue describes the change. Those pull requests are where the code is reviewed.

---

### 🚀 背景描述

有些设置已经能在对话里改。Agent 可以选择已注册的模型、调整思考参数、选择技能或技能库、启用已就绪的连接器、修改本会话的审阅偏好。其余设置仍要打开设置页。

本 issue 要做的是把其余的普通设置也放进这条路径。Agent 提出修改。卡片上显示当前值、新值，以及改完作用在部署、共享资源、Project 还是 Session。用户核对卡片，在对话里确认。之后的任务使用保存后的值。

### 设计思路

沿用已有的配置服务和确认卡片。Agent 先读取当前值、这个值从哪里继承、有哪些允许的选项，然后只提案这些字段。

这条路径要覆盖的设置：

1. 包源和 Runner。选择已有的 pip 或 conda 预设。把已注册的 Runner 分配给 Project 或 Session，或取消这项分配。
2. 代理。管理共享代理。选择模型供应商使用的代理，以及 MCP 使用的代理。修改部署的默认路由单独确认。
3. 网页搜索和凭据。在 Native 和 JiuwenSwarm 已经支持的范围内修改搜索、抓取和缓存。已支持供应商的 Key 通过专用输入替换或清除。
4. 审阅、探索树、JSON 预览和继承。选择 Reviewer 是否参与。选择已注册的探索树模板，以及支持的强度和预算。开关 JSON 专用预览。有限的 Project 和 Session 普通设置可以恢复为继承。
5. 安全和审批。修改沙箱网络、当前会话的审批、新会话的默认审批、低风险自动保存。每一项单独确认。
6. 模型和供应商。修改已有模型的说明信息和 API 身份，修改共享供应商的连接及其凭据。保存前核对真正接收凭据的地址。
7. Memory 和 Neo4j。开关工作台记忆图谱。选择本地或 Neo4j。填写地址和用户名。Neo4j 密码单独替换或清除。
8. 已经注册的 MCP。修改说明信息、超时、启用状态和支持的覆盖项。已有的凭据 header 通过专用输入替换。删除自定义服务器单独确认。

权限和安全策略不并进普通确认。密钥只在专用输入里填写。提案、预览和回执里不出现密钥。

本 issue 仍留在设置页的有：新建 MCP、修改 MCP 地址、OAuth、任意 header 或环境变量、导入和安装。注册 Runner 或 SSH、创建运行环境、安装或卸载软件包。插件专有设置。全局 Reviewer Specialist 开关。探索树模板里的自由提示词、评分权重和轮次。

### 涉及的公开接口

扩展已有的对话配置接口：它可以提案哪些能力、提案带哪些字段、一项修改需要哪种确认。发现、预览和保存仍用原来的机制。每项设置保留自己的作用范围、校验和凭据存放位置。绘制卡片的调用方按返回里的能力和确认要求来显示。

### 与其他模块的关系

设置清单、卡片和请求服务是上面每一块共用的。结果要同时适用于 Native 和 JiuwenSwarm，适用于 Project 的值以及继承它的 Session，也适用于已经拍下配置快照的排队任务。代理选择和安全策略会改变网页搜索、模型调用、MCP 和沙箱如何访问网络。一次保存如果必须重连外部服务或重启进程，这一步也算进验收。

### 测试设计与测试计划

启动真实应用。用真实模型，在浏览器对话里对上面每一块设置提出修改、确认、保存、刷新后读回。再跑一个后续任务，确认它用的是新值。需要重启或重连的，把这一步算进去。

拒绝一次权限修改、一次凭据修改、一次代理修改和一次外部连接。密钥不得出现在对话、预览或回执里。

记录代码版本、环境和结果。这些设置合在一起之后，共享的设置清单、卡片和请求服务仍按现在的方式响应。

### 验收标准

- [ ] 上面列出的每项设置都能在对话里提案。卡片显示当前值、新值和作用位置。
- [ ] 权限、安全策略、凭据接收地址、删除自定义服务器，各自单独等待确认。
- [ ] 密钥只在专用输入里填写，不出现在对话、预览或回执里。
- [ ] 保存并刷新后能读回该值，后续任务使用该值。
- [ ] 上面写明留在设置页的那些设置保持不变。
- [ ] 检查记录写明代码版本、环境和结果。

### 补充信息

包源和 Runner 已经在 `main`（#727）。其余几块在 #734、#737、#756、#758、#763、#770、#773。本 issue 描述这次改动。代码审查在这些 pull request 里进行。

openAI API async stream error ... Unsupported gateway parameters: reasoning_split

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: 37a16ef578004480967b344b8c5511e2
Branch: dev1/fix/ime-enter-everywhere
Base: 865102a336d9
At: 2026-11-04T00:04:46Z

## What happens

The fix that landed for the desktop composer (#794 / #804) introduced a single predicate, `commitsOnEnter`, and wired three desktop call sites to it. Six Enter handlers were left behind, and two of the guards that exist are only half a guard. With a Chinese / Japanese / Korean IME the Enter that accepts a candidate still reaches them.

Unguarded on `main` `865102a336d9ed972fd073b7eecbcf10ae79ed4c`:

| Site | What the composition Enter does today |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/web/src/SshKeyFileField.tsx:83` | calls `browse()`, so the dialog leaves the directory the user was typing |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/RunnerResources.tsx:588` | sends a second `GET /api/remote-hosts/key-files` for the half-typed path (1 → 2 requests) |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/Timeouts.tsx:158` | commits the timeout field with the pinyin still in it |
| `apps/desktop/src/views/ModelForm.tsx:199` | applies the highlighted model-listing entry, so the field becomes a value the user did not choose |

Guarded, but only against one of the two shapes an engine reports:

```tsx
// apps/web/src/session/ManagementControls.tsx:66
if (event.key !== "Enter" || event.nativeEvent.isComposing) return;
// apps/web/src/App.tsx:5051
if (event.key !== "Enter" || event.shiftKey || event.nativeEvent.isComposing) return;
```

These read `nativeEvent.isComposing` only. An engine that reports the confirming Enter as `keyCode === 229` without setting `isComposing` (notably on Windows) gets past both, and neither reads a top-level `isComposing` on a bare `KeyboardEvent`.

Both shapes are what `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts` already handles:

```ts
if (event.isComposing === true || event.nativeEvent?.isComposing === true) return false;
if (event.keyCode === 229) return false;
```

Five more handlers share an `Enter`/`Space` branch that only selects or activates something and commits no data (`apps/web/src/MemoryGraphView.tsx:155`, `apps/web/src/IdeaTreeCanvas.tsx:287`, `apps/desktop/src/views/WorkspacePanel.tsx:528`, `apps/desktop/src/views/ToolIoBlock.tsx:69`, `apps/desktop/src/views/settings/ListSelect.tsx:167`). They are listed so the sweep is reproducible, not to change them.

## Expected

An Enter whose keydown belongs to an open composition must not drive a browse, a request, a field commit or a listing pick, in either app. After the composition ends, Enter behaves exactly as it does today, and `Shift+Enter` keeps the meaning each call site already gives it.

## Evidence

Reproduced on `main` `865102a336d9ed972fd073b7eecbcf10ae79ed4c` by rendering the real components with a synthetic keydown carrying `isComposing: true`, `nativeEvent.isComposing: true` and `keyCode: 229`, then the same keydown with `isComposing: false` and `keyCode: 13` as the control.

Web `SshKeyFileField`, the dialog leaves the typed directory:

```
not ok 1 - SshKeyFileField: Enter while an IME is composing must not drive browse()
    a composition Enter must not trigger a browse
    + actual - expected
    + [
    +   '~/.ssh'
    + ]
    - []
```

Desktop `RunnerResources` key-file browser, two requests for one Enter:

```
not ok 1 - desktop SshKeyFileField: Enter while an IME is composing must not browse()
    a composition Enter must not trigger a browse
    2 !== 1
```

Desktop `ModelForm` model listing, a value the user did not pick:

```
not ok 1 - ModelForm combobox: Enter while an IME is composing must not apply a listing entry
    a composition Enter must not apply a listing entry
    'gpt-4o-mini' !== ''
```

Desktop `Timeouts` timeout field, committed without the field ever blurring:

```
not ok 1 - desktop timeout field: Enter while an IME is composing must not commit the field
    a composition Enter must not commit the field
    false !== true
```

Web `ManagementControls` rename, the half-guard the composition flag does not reach — this keydown sets `keyCode: 229` while both `isComposing` flags stay false:

```
not ok 1 - InlineRenameInput: Enter while an IME is composing must not commit the rename
    a composition Enter must not blur the rename field
    false !== true
```

The control case (composition already ended) is green in every one of them, so the failure is the composing path and not the probe.

## Why this is not covered by #804

`#804` changed `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/views/Composer.tsx`, `PromptDialog.tsx` and `Sidebar.tsx` only. `apps/web` keeps its own call sites and never imports from `apps/desktop`, and the two `nativeEvent.isComposing` guards above were already there before that PR, which is what made them look done.

## Acceptance

- Every Enter handler that commits, sends, requests or picks reads one predicate per app: the existing `apps/desktop/src/app/ime-enter.ts` for desktop, and the same predicate in `apps/web` for web, with the two copies kept character-for-character identical and each covered by the same set of unit cases.
- Each of the six sites above has a test that fails on the composition keydown and passes on the post-composition one.
- The five select/activate handlers stay unchanged, and the pull request says why.
- `git grep` for a bare `Enter` keydown comparison in `apps/web/src` and `apps/desktop/src` returns only those five, so a later reader can re-run the sweep the same way.
- Both apps' existing suites stay green.
