828.body:
Implementation: ScienceDiscovery (ours) — PR follows within 24h. Do not pick up without a `pickup-ok` comment on this issue.

Written-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claimed-by: ScienceDiscovery Lead
Claim-Id: 00b72e8906624c64bc21387d07d9e5e8
Branch: dev1/fix/csv-parsed-extra-column
Base: 865102a336d9
At: 2026-11-04T00:05:36Z

## What happens

Two things go wrong in the CSV/TSV importer, both from deciding the table's columns from the rows instead of from the header line:

1. **A column appears that is not in the file.** When a row has more cells than the header, Papa Parse parks the surplus cells on the record under its internal key `__parsed_extra`, and the importer turns that key into a real column titled `__parsed_extra` — sortable, typed, exported. With one surplus cell the value is a plain number; with two or more it is the cells joined by commas (`"3,4"`), i.e. a value the file never contained.
2. **A column that is in the file can vanish.** When no row fills a header column, the row-key union has no such key and the column is absent from `columns` altogether — not empty, not hidden: it cannot be seen, charted or exported.

On `main` `865102a336d9ed972fd073b7eecbcf10ae79ed4c`, `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`:

- `:210` parses with `header: true` (`:212`), so a record wider than the header cannot be keyed by name.
- `:108` decides the columns from the union of the row keys, excluding exactly one synthetic key:

```ts
const fields = [...new Set(rows.flatMap((row) => Object.keys(row)).filter((field) => field !== "__rowId"))];
```

- `:222` does read the real header (`fields = result.meta.fields ?? []`), but only hands it to `inferTableKind`, never to the column list.
- `:157`/`:158` then build a `ColumnProfile` per key, and `VirtualDataTable.tsx:96` renders `column.id` as the header text (`:95` puts it in the sort button's title), so the reader sees the literal key.

The same function is the import path for every CSV/TSV artifact, before anything renders, so no viewer-level workaround exists.

## Steps to reproduce

Any CSV with a row wider or narrower than its header line — no quoting, BOM or header trick involved:

```
a,b
1,2,3
```

and, for the missing-column half:

```
a,b,c
1,2
```

## Expected

The table shows the file's own columns, in the header's order, under the header's own names. Surplus cells never become a column of their own: if they are still shown, they are shown under a header cell that is visibly empty — the way the API's delimited preview already reports a column with no name — never under a name the file did not write. A header column stays present when every row is short of it.

## Actual

Run through the importer itself (`parseCsvText`, `apps/web` at `bd8423b8`), not through Papa Parse directly:

```
=== extra cells (3 in a 2-column row) ===
content: "a,b\n1,2,3\n"
columns: [{"id":"a","label":"a"},{"id":"b","label":"b"},{"id":"__parsed_extra","label":"  parsed extra"}]
rows: [{"__rowId":"row-2","a":1,"b":2,"__parsed_extra":3}]
warnings: ["Row 2: Too many fields: expected 2 fields but parsed 3"]

=== two extra cells (4 in a 2-column row) ===
content: "a,b\n1,2,3,4\n"
columns: [{"id":"a","label":"a"},{"id":"b","label":"b"},{"id":"__parsed_extra","label":"  parsed extra"}]
rows: [{"__rowId":"row-2","a":1,"b":2,"__parsed_extra":"3,4"}]
warnings: ["Row 2: Too many fields: expected 2 fields but parsed 4"]

=== short row (1 in a 3-column row) ===
content: "a,b,c\n1,2\n"
columns: [{"id":"a","label":"a"},{"id":"b","label":"b"}]
rows: [{"__rowId":"row-2","a":1,"b":2}]
warnings: ["Row 2: Too few fields: expected 3 fields but parsed 2"]
```

So `c` is not merely empty in the third case: it is not a column at all, and `3` in the first case is a column of its own headed `__parsed_extra`. The header cell renders that id verbatim (`VirtualDataTable.tsx:96`); the `label` above is not what the table shows. With `a,,c` (an empty name in the header) the importer already produces a column whose id and label are both `""` and the viewer renders it as a nameless column — so an unnamed column is a shape this table already supports and renders correctly.

## Why it matters

The CSV importer is how a reader's own file becomes a table, and the grid is what they trust for "which value belongs to which column". Here a real value is moved out of its position (`3` in `1,2,3` was under no header), presented as `"3,4"` or as a column named after a library internal, and a version of the same file with an empty column silently loses that column from the viewer, the chart field list and the CSV export.

There *is* a per-row warning (`Too many fields: expected 2 fields but parsed 3`) on the table, so the raggedness is not entirely silent — but it reads as a property of the row, and nothing says a column was invented or dropped.

## Known boundaries

- A header that literally contains `__parsed_extra` is not recoverable: Papa Parse overwrites that key with its own bucket, so the two cannot be told apart. Such a column will read empty while its values land in the surplus columns. This is a pre-existing library collision, not something this fix introduces.
- `DataRow` keys must be unique, so the surplus columns need synthetic ids. A synthetic id that collides with a real header name is suffixed (`__extra_1_`) to stay unique. Ids are internal: with the header cell rendering empty for a column that has no reader-facing name, the synthetic id is not what a reader sees.
- The exported header row goes through the same formula neutralisation as the cells, because in the positional shape a header name is a data value. So a legitimate header that starts with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` also gets the `'` prefix — `-log2FC,b` exports as `'-log2FC,b`. That is deliberate: Excel reads `-log2FC` as a formula, and the prefix is the standard text marker (spreadsheet apps do not display it). Splitting the rule per column kind would put the header and its own cells under two different policies.

## Scope

- `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`: `__parsed_extra` must never become a field. Keep the values rather than drop them, matching the API's delimited preview: table width becomes `max(header count, widest returned row)`, the header's own names stay first and in the file's order (taken from `meta.fields`), surplus columns get synthetic ids (`__extra_1`, `__extra_2`, …) with `label: ""`, and a short row keeps every header column (`null` for the cells it did not have, which is the same value an empty cell already produces today). `profileRows` currently derives the column order from the row-key union at `:108`; it needs an optional ordered column list so a surplus column filled by only some rows does not come and go, and so a header column no row fills is still present.
- `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/CsvArtifactWindow.tsx:214`: the export has to become positional. It currently calls `rowsToCsv(rows, table.columns.map((column) => column.id))`, and that helper uses each field as *both* the value key and the header name — so handing it the header text as the field would read `row[""]` (undefined: the surplus value silently disappears from the export) and two unnamed columns would collapse onto the same object key. The fix needs a header row built from the header text and a body built cell-by-cell from `column.id`, e.g. `tableToCsv(rows, columns)` in `chart-spec/filters.ts`; `rowsToCsv` then has no production caller left and can go, with its spreadsheet-formula test moved to the new helper. Header names travel as data values in that shape, so they get the same formula neutralisation as the cells.
- `apps/web/src/csv-artifact/components/VirtualDataTable.tsx:96`: render the id only when `column.label` is non-empty, and the empty string otherwise, so a column with no reader-facing name gets an empty header cell. Real header names are unaffected, because `:158` gives every real field a non-empty label. `:95`'s sort `title` keeps the id: the header cell is empty, but the sort control still needs an accessible name.
- Unit tests beside the importer in `apps/web/tests/` (its tests live there; `CsvArtifact.test.tsx` already drives the importer through the component, so a focused test may be a new file next to it): one surplus cell and two (no `__parsed_extra` id, header names and order unchanged, values still reachable), a header column that no row fills (present, `null`, `missingCount` counted), the rendered header text for an unnamed column, and the export header, plus the existing well-formed cases unchanged.
- No i18n string is added, no existing column label or header text changes, `#654`'s BOM handling of real header names is untouched, and the `rowId` de-duplication below `:108` is untouched.

Related but separate: `#650`/`#653` fixed quoting in the API preview; the API's own ragged-row normalisation is handled in `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`. This report is the web-side half, and the two should agree on the "no name, values kept" shape.
828.title: [Bug] The web CSV viewer shows a synthetic __parsed_extra column and can hide a real one

835.body:
## Context

This tracks a staged landing for the work currently visible in #315 (GitCode !125), plus the two smaller follow-up branches for KE/trace integration and finish-gate refinements.

The current combined PR is 275 files and about +54k lines. Review feedback has correctly identified both the review/merge risk and the need for an explicit product decision about KE as a first-class ScienceDiscovery surface. I will preserve #315 as the full implementation reference, but stop refreshing it with large upstream merges and instead prepare clean, independently reviewable PRs from current `main`.

## Proposed landing sequence

### A. Independent research/runtime foundations

These do not require the KE service and can be reviewed on their own merits.

- [ ] **A1 — Tool-output trust boundary:** per-run nonce fencing, `untrustedCategory`, MCP remote classification, and the corresponding prompt contract. Raw stored output remains unchanged; fencing applies to model-visible content.
- [ ] **A2 — Research state:** session research state, project ledger hydration/promotion, and tournament ranking primitives.
- [ ] **A3 — Runtime controls:** native stall guard and the `TurnLifecycle.beforeFinish`/continuation event primitives. This will not claim equivalent native-style stall protection for JiuwenSwarm.
- [ ] **A4 — Session Plan:** versioned human approval, decision log, cancellation and recovery, with an explicit compatibility rule for the existing `update_plan` snapshot mechanism.
- [ ] **A5 — Finish-gate core:** skill audit and termination intervention for native and post-run/Swarm execution. The initial landing will include the already-developed fixes for loaded-skill-only audits, Swarm tool aliases, and self-referential gate/verifier text. KE grounding comes later.
- [ ] **A6 — Agent Memory:** candidate memories, human promotion, reviewed-only prompt injection, and background review. The KE LLM-helper dependency and process-global manager need to be removed first.

### B. Knowledge Engine core

- [ ] **B1 — Text/extraction/resolution domain:** pure text, JATS, extraction, and entity-resolution modules with unit tests.
- [ ] **B2 — Graph/growth/eval algorithms:** graph algorithms, gap discovery, growth selection, and evaluation primitives.
- [ ] **B3 — Persistence and ingestion data plane:** SQLite store/migrations, scholarly connectors, PDF/vision parsing, and background runners.
- [ ] **B4 — Orchestration and minimal REST:** orchestrator, grow, routes, and narrowly scoped bootstrap/http wiring. Agent tools, resident summary, graph mirror, and living review stay out of this first REST PR.
- [ ] **B5 — Minimal KE Web shell:** API client, KE page, graph canvas, and document reader.

### C. Agent integration and advanced KE surfaces

- [ ] **C1 — Consumption tools and kbScope:** KE search/expand/grep tools, session binding, web-search restrictions, resident summary, and picker. Scope enforcement lands with the first exposed tool.
- [ ] **C2 — Citation and anti-hallucination runtime:** citation verification, novelty checks, evidence ledger, report polish, and finish-gate grounding. Includes the no-available-KB advisory behavior rather than an unachievable hard lock.
- [ ] **C3 — Reports, DRIFT, and memory-graph bridge:** community reports, DRIFT search, KE-to-memory-graph mirroring, and KB deep links.

### Small follow-ups from the former KE/trace and finish-gate PRs

These can land as soon as their specific dependencies are present; they do not all need to wait for the entire base series.

- [ ] Paper presence lookup and KB badge (after minimal REST + Web).
- [ ] Explicit Paper-to-KB re-ingest (after presence lookup).
- [ ] Reviewer citation checks with a bound-KB short circuit (after citation verification + kbScope).
- [ ] KB reader back-link to the current session memory graph (after graph mirroring).
- [ ] `gap_candidates` to deduplicated `research_state` open questions (after research state + observer wiring).
- [ ] Quoting-discipline skill updates and catalog/version pins with their corresponding gate/skill stages.

## Per-stage requirements

- Each PR is cut from current `main`; mixed files such as `store.ts`, `runs/index.ts`, `http/index.ts`, and `App.tsx` are ported by focused hunks rather than copied wholesale.
- Unit/integration tests and the relevant journeys land with their feature, not in a final test-only PR.
- Current-main behavior is preserved, including catalog transaction/rollback semantics, deletion-settling shutdown, response identity, and Swarm skill-selection behavior.
- Tool trust is field-aware: deterministic verdicts must not implicitly make corpus titles, abstracts, snippets, or entity descriptions trusted.
- The fenced evidence-ledger path, post-run terminal-event ordering, and no-engine kbScope behavior receive explicit integration coverage.
- Runtime-affecting stages receive a clean deployment and real E2E validation before the next stage.

Unless maintainers prefer a dedicated integration branch, the default is small PRs directly to `main`, with at most one or two open at a time. Feedback on the staged product scope and on starting with **A1 + B1** would be appreciated.

837.author: HugoXK
837.body:
## What happens

`apps/web/tests/` holds 126 `*.test.ts` / `*.test.tsx` files, and no TypeScript configuration in the repository includes any of them. The suite runs under `tsx`, which strips the annotations without checking them; the package `typecheck` and the root test type-check both look elsewhere. A type error in a web test therefore cannot turn CI red: `pnpm typecheck` — the `check:typecheck` gate — stays green.

## Where

1. `apps/web/package.json:9` — `"test": "tsx --test tests/*.test.ts tests/*.test.tsx"`. `tsx` transpiles and runs; it does not type-check.
2. `apps/web/tsconfig.json:9` — `"include": ["src/**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx", "vite.config.ts"]`. The package's `typecheck` script (`apps/web/package.json:10`, `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`) therefore cannot see `tests/`.
3. `tsconfig.tests.json:23-28` — its `include` names `packages/*/src/**/*.test.ts(x)` and `services/*/src/**/*.test.ts(x)` only. Its own comment (`tsconfig.tests.json:13-15`) states: "`apps/web` is not here: its tests sit in `tests/`, which its own `include` (`src/**`) never reached, so the base exclude takes nothing away from it." The root `typecheck` script (`package.json:51`) ends with `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`, so the one configuration meant to own test files leaves the web tests out on purpose.

CI runs that script as `check:typecheck` (`test/support/tagged/checks.mjs:23` → `pnpm typecheck`), so this is a hole in a required gate, not just in a local command.

## Measured on `main` at `5c893570`

- 126 files match `apps/web/tests/*.test.ts(x)` (git tree).
- `tsc -p apps/web/tsconfig.json --listFilesOnly` lists 0 files under `apps/web/tests/`.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --listFilesOnly` lists 0 files under `apps/web/tests/` (1,805 files listed in total).
- A throwaway config extending `apps/web/tsconfig.json` with `"exclude": []` and `"include": ["tests/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.tsx"]` lists exactly the 126 files and reports 444 `error TS` diagnostics across 71 files (10 in `.test.ts`, 434 in `.test.tsx`). Those diagnostics are latent today; nothing in CI can see them.

## How to reproduce

1. Append `const notAString: string = 42;` to any `apps/web/tests/*.test.ts`.
2. `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` — exits 0: `tsx` runs the file and never checks the annotation.
3. `pnpm typecheck` — still exits 0: neither configuration includes the file.

## Suggested fix

Give the web tests an owner and a gate:

- Add `apps/web/tsconfig.tests.json` extending `apps/web/tsconfig.json` with `"exclude": []` and `"include": ["tests/**/*.test.ts", "tests/**/*.test.tsx"]`, and run it from the package `typecheck` (or from the root `typecheck` right after `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`). Adding `apps/web/tests/**` to the root `tsconfig.tests.json` include is the alternative, but that config extends `tsconfig.base.json`, not the web package's settings, so it would need the jsx / DOM / `vite/client` options that belong to `apps/web` — a second config is the cleaner shape.
- The 444 existing diagnostics have to be fixed for the gate to pass. If that is too large for one change, stage it: enable `tests/**/*.test.ts` first (10 diagnostics) and `tests/**/*.test.tsx` (434) in a follow-up. Enabling the config while it reports errors leaves the gate red and is not mergeable.

Acceptance: with the new config wired into `pnpm typecheck`, the deliberate `const notAString: string = 42;` makes `pnpm typecheck` (and therefore `check:typecheck`) fail naming that file and line, while `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test` keeps its current behaviour.
837.title: [Bug] The apps/web test suite is never type-checked

839.author: HugoXK
839.body:
## What happens

A delimited dataset preview (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `parseDelimitedTable`) takes its width from the **widest line of the whole file**, so one outlier line decides how many columns every returned row shows. A two-column file that contains a single line with 200,001 fields renders as 1,001 columns, 999 of them carrying an empty header and an empty cell in every row.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): `const widest = lines.reduce(...)`, `const totalColumns = Math.max(header.length, widest)`, `const width = Math.min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS)` (`MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1001`), and the blank header names built at `columns: header.length >= width ? header.slice(0, width) : [...header, ...Array.from({length: width - header.length}, () => "")]`.

## Measured at `0477d328` (default `maxRows`)

- two-column header plus one line of 200,001 fields: `columns 1001`, `clippedColumns {total: 200001, shown: 1001}`, rows padded to 1001 cells each, so 999 columns and ~99,900 cells in the payload are blank.
- the same file without the outlier line: `columns 2`.

## Why it matters

The preview is widened by a line that is not part of the returned rows, and the extra columns carry no header - the grid shows a two-column table as a 1,001-column one. `clippedColumns` does report `{total, shown}`, so the cut is signalled, but the blank columns themselves are still rendered.

## Suggested fix

Cap the *unnamed surplus* columns the way the CSV importer already does (`apps/web/src/csv-artifact/csv/inferCsv.ts`, `surplusColumnLimit`: `min(16, max(2, header.length))`) while never capping header columns, and keep reporting the dropped cells in `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns`.
839.title: [Bug] One outlier line sets a delimited preview's width, so a two-column file renders 1,001 mostly-blank columns

840.author: HugoXK
840.body:
## What happens

The delimited-preview payload carries a `warnings: string[]` field that no consumer reads, and which duplicates text the client already composes and localizes.

## Where

- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` (at `0477d328`): the `warnings` array is built at the end of `parseDelimitedTable` ("The file has {total} columns; the preview shows the first {shown}." and "{n} cells past the preview width are not shown.") and returned in the payload type (`:161`-ish in that revision).
- `apps/web/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` mirrors the field in the web payload type.
- The viewer does not use it: `ArtifactModal` passes `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` down and `DatasetTable` composes its own sentences from `artifact.tableClippedColumns` / `artifact.tableClippedCells` (`apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx`).

## Why it matters

Two places decide what the user is told about a clipped preview: the server strings are English-only, so a Chinese UI would drift from them the moment anyone read them, and a future consumer could show untranslated text. Today the field is dead weight in every preview payload.

## Suggested fix

Either drop `warnings` from the payload and keep `clippedColumns` / `clippedCells` as the only source of truth (the client already localizes from them), or make the client render the server strings through the i18n layer. Pick one owner for the copy.
840.title: [Cleanup] The delimited preview payload's `warnings` field duplicates the client copy, is not localized, and has no consumer

841.author: HugoXK
841.body:
## What happens

`GET` artifact version preview (`services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts`, `buildArtifactVersionPreview` → `parseDelimitedTable` / `recordArrayTable`) now bounds its payload with two server-side constants:

- `const maxRows = Math.min(MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS, parsePositiveInt(maxRowsParam, DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS));` — `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = DEFAULT_MAX_ROWS = 100` (`artifact-dashboard.ts:719` at `0477d328`)
- `const width = Math.min(totalColumns, MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS);` — `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1_001` (`artifact-dashboard.ts:398`)

A caller that asks for more gets less, with no error: the response just carries `truncated` and `clippedColumns`/`clippedCells`.

## Measured at `0477d328`

- 1,500-column CSV → `columns 1001`, `clippedColumns {shown 1001, total 1500}`, `clippedCells 499` (named columns past 1,001 are dropped).
- 401-row CSV at `?maxRows=400` → `rows 100`, `totalRows 400`, `truncated true`.
- 500-record JSON at `?maxRows=400` → the same 100 rows (the clamp applies to the record-array path too).

## Why it matters

The bundled web client never sends `maxRows` (`apps/web/src/api/artifacts.ts:201` forwards an optional value only, and `apps/desktop` reads local CSV), so there is no in-repo regression — but for any other API caller this is a silent contract change: asking for 400 rows returns 100, and a legitimately wide table loses named columns. `#829` asked for a preview that keeps every row as wide as the columns it advertises; the bound is what makes the payload finite, so the trade is deliberate — it is the *silence* that needs a decision.

Two questions to settle, and then to write down where a caller can find them:

1. Should `maxRows` above the server constant be rejected (400 with a stated limit) instead of clamped, or should `truncated` stay the only signal?
2. Should the preview document the row limit and the column limit (with `clippedColumns`/`clippedCells` as the reporting half) in the API docs, and should a caller be able to learn both limits without probing?

Related: `#829` (the shear this bound fixes), `#839` (the width rule taken from the widest line), `#840` (the payload `warnings` field has no consumer).

## Suggested fix

Decide the two questions above, then either reject over-limit `maxRows` with a stated maximum or document the clamp; document `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS` and `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS` (and that a wider/taller request is clipped, not failed) in the API reference, so an outside caller can size its request without probing.
841.title: [Bug] The artifact preview endpoint silently clamps `?maxRows=` to 100 and caps the column set at 1,001, so an outside API caller gets less than it asked for

842.author: HugoXK
842.body:
## What happens

A delimited dataset preview is capped at `MAX_PREVIEW_COLUMNS = 1_001` columns and `MAX_PREVIEW_ROWS = 100` rows, and the payload reports what left the preview (`clippedColumns {total, shown}`, `clippedCells`, `warnings`). The viewer renders that report only through `DatasetTable` — and `.csv` artifacts never render `DatasetTable`.

## Where (at `981fdf51`, the merge commit of `#830`)

- `apps/web/src/csvArtifact.ts:73-82` — `detectCsvArtifact` sends every `.csv` name, `text/csv` media type or CSV-looking content to the CSV viewer.
- `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:874` — `artifact?.kind === "dataset" && csvDetection && !(structureFormat && source)` renders `CsvArtifactPreview` (`:205`), not the dataset table.
- `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:831-832` — `clippedCells` / `clippedColumns` are passed only to `DatasetTable` (`:239`, meta line at `:254`).
- `services/api/src/artifact-dashboard.ts` — the JSON record-array path always returns `clippedCells: 0` and `clippedColumns {shown: total}`, so `.tsv` (and generally delimited content that is not detected as CSV) is the only kind whose clipped numbers reach a reader.

## Measured

- A `.csv` artifact with 200,001-field lines: the API preview comes back `1001` columns / `clippedColumns {shown: 1001, total: 200001}`, and the artifact panel shows only the "open CSV workspace" card — none of the new text, because the CSV workspace parses the source client-side.
- The same content saved as `.tsv`: `DatasetTable` renders `1 row (showing 1001 of 200001 columns) (N cells past the preview width are not shown)`.

## Why it matters

`#830`'s stated contract is that clipping "is reported, not silent" — and for the most common delimited artifact kind (`.csv`) the reader is told nothing. The new i18n strings (`artifact.tableClippedColumns`, `artifact.tableClippedCells`) and the two props have no reachable CSV path.

## Suggested fix

Either pass the clipped numbers into `CsvArtifactPreview` / the CSV workspace window and render the same meta line there, or render the dataset table for a CSV artifact whose payload was clipped. One signal per loss, no duplicate sentences; keep the CSV workspace's own surplus-column handling (`csv.importSurplusColumns`) separate from this panel-level notice.

Related: `#839` (the width rule that creates the mismatch), `#840` (the payload `warnings` field has no consumer), `#841` (`maxRows` / column-cap contract for outside API callers).
842.title: [Bug] The clipped-preview notice never reaches `.csv` readers: the CSV panel renders no column or cell clip signal

844.author: nanzhaogang
844.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

Both clients (`apps/web` and `apps/desktop`) can fail in ways a user cannot describe from memory: a stuck run, a wrong artifact, an offline shell. Today the only way to report one is to leave the app, open GitHub, and write an issue from scratch — which loses the version, OS, locale and the failure state the app itself already knows. Error surfaces (including the "cannot reach the local service" screen) end in a dead end with no way to say anything.

This issue tracks the full delivery: a shared submission contract, a Cloudflare Worker that relays reports into a private GitHub issue, a feedback dialog in both front ends, an entry point on the offline screen that seeds the dialog with the failure's diagnostics, and a receipt code the user can quote when following up.

Related: the desktop shell must not be left out of a feature that only lands in `apps/web`; the offline screen is the surface that has no report path at all today.

Related pull request: branch `feat/user-feedback` — feature implementation, tests and deployment notes.

## Design Ideas

- **One contract, three consumers.** Payload building, redaction, PII detection, field validation and receipt generation live in `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts` and are imported by `apps/web`, `apps/desktop` and the Worker. The wire format cannot drift between the two clients and the server.
- **Triage fields are required.** Frequency (always / sometimes / once) and impact (blocks me / slows my work / affects the experience) are mandatory: a report without them cannot be routed or prioritized, so the dialog keeps 提交 disabled and states why, rather than accepting an untriaged issue.
- **A receipt instead of an account.** A submission returns `FB-XXXX-XXXX`, drawn from a 32-symbol alphabet (no `I/O/0/1`) to stay readable over the phone. It is shown once, kept in local history, and is what support asks for.
- **Diagnostics on by default, redacted on the way out.** Key names are forced to `[REDACTED:key]`, Windows profile paths are normalized, and the user can uncheck the block. The offline screen pre-fills diagnostics with boot state, origin and user agent so a "cannot connect" report arrives with evidence attached.
- **PII is advisory, not a wall.** Phone numbers, ID cards and emails in the description raise a confirmation step instead of silently rewriting the text, because the user may be quoting exactly what broke.
- **Draft and history stay local.** The draft is written to `localStorage` on every change and restored on reopen; the last 50 submissions live beside it. Nothing is stored server-side except the issue itself.
- **Abuse control belongs to the relay, not the client.** Keyed dedupe for seven days, a per-IP hourly limit, a per-install daily limit and a daily issue quota keep a public endpoint from becoming a spam funnel — and a duplicate returns the original receipt instead of creating a second issue.
- **The token never ships.** The GitHub PAT lives as a Cloudflare secret; the bundle only knows the Worker URL.

## Involved Public APIs

One new endpoint, on the Worker (not on the product's REST service): `POST /api/feedback`.

- Request: `{ v: 1, clientTs, kind, title, body, contact?, meta, diagnostics? }`; `v` is the contract version and `clientTs` an ISO timestamp. `kind ∈ {bug, idea, other}`; `contact` is `{ type: "email" | "github", value }`; body 10–2000 characters (its UTF-8 size is checked before sending); title capped at 120; diagnostics capped at 4000; the whole request capped at 16 KiB.
- Response `201 { receipt, createdAt }`. Failures are `{ error }` objects: `400 invalid` (with a `fields` map) or `400 invalid_json`, `403 forbidden`, `409 duplicate` (carries the original receipt), `413 too_large`, `429 rate_limited`, `502 upstream_failed`, `503 unavailable`. No issue URL is returned — the tracker issue lives in a private repository.
- CORS: an explicit origin allowlist, configurable through `ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, covering the local dev ports of both clients.
- Endpoint constant: `FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT` / `FEEDBACK_API_PATH` in `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`.

No route of `services/api` changes; the clients do not proxy feedback through the local backend, so reporting still works when the backend is down.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/operational-logging`: new `feedback` entry point (contract, validation, redaction, receipts, PII) and its reuse of the existing `redaction` and `diagnostics` helpers.
- `packages/feedback-worker`: new workspace package — Worker entry, GitHub issue creation, KV-backed limits, mock-GitHub tests.
- `apps/web`: dialog, API client mapping status codes to user-facing failures, draft/history store, entries in the header and in `ErrorDiagnosticActions`.
- `apps/desktop`: the same dialog and store, a 我要反馈 entry in the sidebar footer to the right of the GitHub star, and an entry on the offline screen that pre-fills diagnostics; the dialog is mounted in the offline branch so that entry works.
- Internationalization: every string lands in `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` and in both `apps/desktop/src/text/zh.ts` and `en.ts`; the two dictionaries must stay structurally identical.
- Infrastructure: a `FEEDBACK_KV` namespace and a `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret on Cloudflare; labels `source:in-app`, `kind:<kind>`, `needs-triage` on created issues.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- **Unit tests (47 cases across 6 files):**
  - `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.test.ts` (8): receipt format and 100k uniqueness, redaction of keyed values and profile paths, advisory PII detection, contact classification, title derivation, payload building, field validation.
  - `packages/feedback-worker/src/index.test.ts` (9): CORS preflight and disallowed origin, 16 KiB rejection before parsing, 400 on bad JSON/fields, success path creating an issue, 409 duplicate within the window, per-install daily 429, daily quota 503, GitHub 5xx surfacing 502 without leaking the token.
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackApi.test.ts` (8) and `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-submit.test.ts` (8): status-code to failure mapping in each client.
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackStore.test.ts` (7) and `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-store.test.ts` (7): install id persistence, draft default and round-trip, corrupt-data fallback, history capped at 50, removal by receipt.
- **Component tests:** not yet written. The required-field rule (`frequency` and `impact` both chosen before submit) is currently covered by manual verification only; the plan is to extract the form-state predicate out of the dialog into a shared pure function and assert it from both apps.
- **End-to-end (manual, against the deployed Worker):** submit from the desktop dialog → receipt shown and recorded in 我的反馈; stop the local backend, reload, land on the offline screen → 我要反馈 → description pre-filled and diagnostics expandable → submit → receipt; restart the backend → 重试 recovers in one click. Verified receipts: `FB-775M-N8A8` (normal), `FB-XKXW-FGSZ` (from the offline screen).
- **Regression:** the offline screen still renders exactly as before when no feedback is submitted; ordinary sessions are untouched; the web feedback dialog behaves identically to the desktop one.

Commands that must pass: `pnpm check` (architecture check, typecheck, unit tests); `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test`; `pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report can be submitted from `apps/web` and from `apps/desktop`, and a GitHub issue is created with `source:in-app`, `kind:<kind>` and `needs-triage`.
- [ ] Frequency and impact are mandatory in both clients: an untouched form keeps 提交 disabled and shows 出现频率和影响程度为必填项.
- [ ] The receipt shown after submission matches the one in 我的反馈 and the issue body.
- [ ] The offline screen's 我要反馈 opens the dialog with the failure text pre-filled and diagnostics available (not "本条反馈没有可用诊断信息").
- [ ] A submission from the offline screen still succeeds while the local backend is down.

## Additional Information

Deployed endpoint: `https://sciencediscovery-feedback.sciencediscovery.workers.dev` (Cloudflare requires the `<worker>.<subdomain>.workers.dev` form). KV namespace `FEEDBACK_KV`; secrets `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `REPO_OWNER`, `REPO_NAME`; deployment via `npx wrangler deploy` from `packages/feedback-worker`. Deployment and verification steps are in `packages/feedback-worker/README.md`.

---

## 🚀 背景描述

两端客户端（`apps/web` 与 `apps/desktop`）都会出现用户无法靠记忆描述清楚的故障：运行卡住、产物不对、本地服务连不上。今天要反馈这类问题，用户必须先离开应用、打开 GitHub、从零写一个 issue——版本、系统、语言、当时的故障状态全部丢失，而这些信息应用本身就有。报错界面（包括「连不上本地服务」那一页）是个死胡同，用户没有地方说一句话。

本 issue 跟踪完整交付：共享的提交契约、把反馈转成私有 GitHub issue 的 Cloudflare Worker、两端一致的反馈对话框、在离线页把故障诊断预填进对话框的入口，以及用户可以引用的回执码。

相关：一个只落在 `apps/web` 的功能，不应把桌面端漏掉；而离线页正是目前完全没有反馈入口的地方。

相关 PR：分支 `feat/user-feedback`——功能实现、测试与部署说明。

## 设计思路

- **一份契约、三个使用方。** payload 构造、脱敏、PII 检测、字段校验与回执生成集中在 `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts`，由 `apps/web`、`apps/desktop` 与 Worker 共同引用，两端与服务的线上格式不会漂移。
- **分诊字段必填。** 出现频率（总是 / 偶尔 / 仅一次）与影响程度（无法使用 / 影响工作效率 / 影响使用体验）为必填项：缺少这两项的报告无法定级与派发，因此对话框在未选时保持「提交」禁用并说明原因，而不是收下一条无法分诊的 issue。
- **用回执码，而不是账号。** 提交返回 `FB-XXXX-XXXX`，字符集剔除 `I/O/0/1` 以便口头转述；提交成功时展示一次，并保留在本地历史里，客服只需要这个码。
- **诊断信息默认附带、出口前脱敏。** 键名强制为 `[REDACTED:key]`，Windows 用户目录路径归一化，用户可以取消勾选。离线页会自动带上启动状态、origin 与 user agent，让「连不上」这类报告自带证据。
- **PII 只提示、不拦截。** 描述里的手机号、身份证、邮箱触发一次确认，而不是偷偷改写文本——用户可能正是在引用出错的内容。
- **草稿与历史留在本地。** 草稿随输入写入 `localStorage`，下次打开恢复；最近 50 条提交记录与之并列。服务端除 issue 本身外不存任何内容。
- **限流属于中继，不属于客户端。** 七天内的去重、按 IP 的小时限流、按 installId 的日限流与每日 issue 配额，防止公开端点变成垃圾入口；重复内容返回原回执码，不再开第二个 issue。
- **Token 永不进包。** GitHub PAT 存在 Cloudflare secret 里，前端只知道 Worker 地址。

## 涉及的公共 API

新增一个端点，位于 Worker（不落在产品 REST 服务上）：`POST /api/feedback`。

- 请求：`{ v: 1, clientTs, kind, title, body, contact?, meta, diagnostics? }`；`v` 为契约版本，`clientTs` 为 ISO 时间戳。`kind ∈ {bug, idea, other}`；`contact` 为 `{ type: "email" | "github", value }`；正文 10–2000 字（发送前按 UTF-8 字节校验）；标题上限 120；诊断上限 4000；整个请求上限 16 KiB。
- 响应 `201 { receipt, createdAt }`。失败统一为 `{ error }` 对象：`400 invalid`（附 `fields` 明细）或 `400 invalid_json`、`403 forbidden`、`409 duplicate`（带原回执码）、`413 too_large`、`429 rate_limited`、`502 upstream_failed`、`503 unavailable`。不返回 issue 链接——追踪 issue 位于私有仓库。
- CORS：显式 origin 白名单，可通过 `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` 配置，默认覆盖两端本地开发端口。
- 端点常量：`packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.ts` 中的 `FEEDBACK_ENDPOINT` / `FEEDBACK_API_PATH`。

`services/api` 的路由不变；两端不经过本地后端转发反馈，因此本地服务挂掉时仍可提交。

## 与其他模块的关联

- `packages/operational-logging`：新增 `feedback` 入口（契约、校验、脱敏、回执、PII），复用既有的 `redaction` 与 `diagnostics`。
- `packages/feedback-worker`：新增 workspace 包——Worker 入口、GitHub issue 创建、KV 限流、基于 mock GitHub 的测试。
- `apps/web`：对话框、把状态码映射为用户可读失败原因的 API 客户端、草稿/历史存储、头部入口与 `ErrorDiagnosticActions` 中的入口。
- `apps/desktop`：同一套对话框与存储、侧栏底部 GitHub 星标右侧的「我要反馈」入口，以及离线页上预填诊断的入口；对话框在离线分支同样挂载，保证该入口可用。
- 国际化：新增文案同时进入 `apps/web/src/i18n/messages.ts` 与 `apps/desktop` 的 `text/zh.ts`、`en.ts`，两份字典结构必须完全一致。
- 基础设施：Cloudflare 上的 `FEEDBACK_KV` namespace 与 `GITHUB_TOKEN` secret；新建 issue 打上 `source:in-app`、`kind:<kind>`、`needs-triage` 标签。

## 测试设计与测试计划

- **单元测试（6 个文件、47 个用例）：**
  - `packages/operational-logging/src/feedback.test.ts`（8）：回执码格式与 10 万次唯一性、键值脱敏与路径归一化、PII 提示不改原文、联系方式分类、标题推导、payload 构造、字段校验。
  - `packages/feedback-worker/src/index.test.ts`（9）：CORS 预检与非法来源、解析前拒绝 16 KiB、非法 JSON/字段 400、成功建 issue、窗口内重复 409、installId 日限 429、每日配额 503、GitHub 5xx 返回 502 且不泄露 token。
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackApi.test.ts`（8）与 `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-submit.test.ts`（8）：两端各自的状态码到失败类型映射。
  - `apps/web/tests/FeedbackStore.test.ts`（7）与 `apps/desktop/tests/feedback-store.test.ts`（7）：installId 持久化、草稿默认值与往返、脏数据回退、历史上限 50、按回执码删除。
- **组件测试：** 尚未编写。必填项规则（未选出现频率与影响程度时不可提交）目前只有人工验证覆盖；计划把对话框里的表单状态判断抽成共享纯函数，两端各写断言。
- **端到端（人工，对已部署 Worker）：** 桌面端对话框提交 → 展示回执码且「我的反馈」有记录；停掉本地后端并刷新 → 进入离线页 →「我要反馈」→ 描述已预填、诊断可展开 → 提交 → 得到回执码；恢复后端 → 点「重试」一次即恢复。已验证回执码：`FB-775M-N8A8`（正常）、`FB-XKXW-FGSZ`（离线页）。
- **回归：** 不提交反馈时离线页与改动前完全一致；普通会话不受影响；Web 与桌面端对话框行为一致。

必须通过的命令：`pnpm check`（架构检查、类型检查、单元测试）；`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/web test`；`pnpm --filter @sciencediscovery/desktop test`。

## 验收标准

- [ ] `apps/web` 与 `apps/desktop` 均可提交反馈，并创建带 `source:in-app`、`kind:<kind>`、`needs-triage` 的 GitHub issue。
- [ ] 两端的出现频率与影响程度均为必填：未选择时「提交」保持禁用，并显示「出现频率和影响程度为必填项」。
- [ ] 提交后展示的回执码与「我的反馈」记录、issue 正文中的一致。
- [ ] 离线页的「我要反馈」打开对话框时描述已预填，诊断信息可用（不是「本条反馈没有可用诊断信息」）。
- [ ] 本地后端停止时，从离线页提交仍然成功。

## 补充信息

已部署端点：`https://sciencediscovery-feedback.sciencediscovery.workers.dev`（Cloudflare 固定为 `<worker>.<子域名>.workers.dev` 形式）。KV namespace `FEEDBACK_KV`；secrets `GITHUB_TOKEN`、`REPO_OWNER`、`REPO_NAME`；在 `packages/feedback-worker` 下执行 `npx wrangler deploy` 部署。部署与验证步骤见 `packages/feedback-worker/README.md`。

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Deleting a model is rejected if an existing session references it.

**Steps to reproduce**
1. Create a session using a configured model.
2. Try to delete that model.
3. Deletion is rejected because the model is used by the session.

**Expected behavior**

Allow deleting a model even if it is used by existing sessions or configured as the global default model.

- Preserve all historical sessions and messages. Do not silently switch an affected session to another model.
- Clear the deleted model's global-default reference (leaving no default until the user explicitly configures one). New sessions should prompt for model selection when no default exists.
- When reopening an affected session, keep its history visible and ask the user to explicitly select an available model before continuing.
- Handle invalid model references consistently after restarting or reloading the app; never silently fall back to the first listed model.
- If Project-level model overrides can reference the deleted model, handle them without blocking deletion and without an unannounced provider/model switch.

**Acceptance criteria**
- [ ] Deleting a model succeeds when it is referenced by historical sessions, set as the global default, or both.
- [ ] All affected session histories remain accessible.
- [ ] No arbitrary replacement model is selected for affected sessions or the global default.
- [ ] Reopening or reloading affected sessions offers a clear path to select/configure a model before the next run.
- [ ] A new session without a global default asks for model selection.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

ScienceDiscovery Web UI.

### Version Information

Branch: `main`
Commit: `0b2479200cf2f94a105e8d33427732266cbbcddb`

### Additional Information

This behavior is included in the v0.4.0-rc1 release scope: #718.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Desktop run failure alerts currently expose raw technical error messages, mix Chinese and English, and can repeat information for the same failure.

**Example (Chinese UI):** An Agent idle timeout displays both:
- `运行失败（timeout）：Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 1000 ms`
- `超时：Request stopped because the Agent idle timeout was reached after 1 seconds. Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 1000 ms`

**Steps to reproduce**
1. In **System configuration → Timeouts**, temporarily set the Agent idle timeout to 1 second.
2. Start a session run that takes longer than the timeout without gateway progress.
3. Inspect the failure notices in the Desktop conversation.
4. Restore the original timeout setting afterward.

**Expected behavior**
- Present a clear, localized failure summary with actionable recovery guidance.
- Avoid redundant user-facing alerts for the same failure.
- Keep raw diagnostics available in an expandable technical-details area.
- Apply consistent presentation to existing run failure types (timeout, unauthorized, rate-limited, transport-error, server-error, invalid-tool-call, semantic-error).

### Detailed Environment Information Description

ScienceDiscovery Desktop, Chinese UI.

### Version Information

Branch: `main`
Commit: `0b2479200cf2f94a105e8d33427732266cbbcddb`

### Additional Information

- Related release requirement: #718.
- Scope: **Desktop failure-alert presentation** (content and visual hierarchy). Web should follow the same user-facing principles, but a full Web UI redesign and backend error-classification changes are out of scope.
- Web also displays raw technical error text; Desktop is the primary focus of this report.

847.author: HugoXK
847.body:
## Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed in the latest version.
- [x] The reproduction below is minimal, self-contained, and includes the observed result.

## 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

**Current:** when a workspace transfer copies a directory, the Activity panel's transfer row reports the *number of declared mappings* as the file total while the committed count comes from the *expanded* files, so a directory of three files reads `3/1 files committed`.

**Expected:** `3/3 files committed` — the total is the number of files the transfer is actually copying.

### Where

`apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx:103` (read on `main` `c4f5ecb36ca0439d8e45cc30f1e8d0210413ea70`):

```tsx
<small>{t("activity.filesCommitted", { committed: item.progress.filter((file) => file.state === "completed").length, total: item.files.length })}</small>
```

`item.files` is the transfer *request* — 1-50 explicit mappings, where one mapping may be a directory (`packages/schema/src/workspace-transfer.ts:6`). `item.progress` is the expanded per-file work list (`workspace-transfer.ts:14`), and the API builds it by expanding every mapping into one entry per file (`services/api/src/workspace-transfers.ts:107-115`):

```ts
job.progress = job.files.flatMap((file) => {
  const selected = entries.filter((item) => item.path === file.sourcePath || item.path.startsWith(`${file.sourcePath}/`));
  ...
  return selected.map((entry) => ({ ... }));
});
```

So `progress.length` is the file count and `files.length` is the mapping count; the numerator and the denominator count different things. The same panel already renders `item.progress` as the file list (`AgentActivityPanel.tsx:105`), so the denominator contradicts the list right below it.

### Red-first reproduction (fails on `main` `c4f5ecb`)

Minimal self-contained test, rendered with `react-test-renderer` and a stubbed `ApiClient` — one declared directory mapping, three expanded completed files:

```tsx
const activity = { executions: [], timers: [], agents: [], transfers: [{
  id: "t1", sessionId: "session", agentId: "main", state: "completed",
  sourceWorkspaceId: "ws_a", targetWorkspaceId: "ws_b",
  files: [{ sourcePath: "data", targetPath: "data" }],
  createdAt: "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  progress: [
    { sourcePath: "data/a.csv", targetPath: "data/a.csv", size: 1, sha256: "a".repeat(64), bytes: 1, state: "completed" },
    { sourcePath: "data/b.csv", targetPath: "data/b.csv", size: 1, sha256: "b".repeat(64), bytes: 1, state: "completed" },
    { sourcePath: "data/c.csv", targetPath: "data/c.csv", size: 1, sha256: "c".repeat(64), bytes: 1, state: "completed" },
  ],
}] };
const client = { getAgentActivity: async () => activity } as unknown as ApiClient;
await act(async () => { view = create(createElement(AgentActivityPanel, { client, sessionId: "session" })); });
assert.match(JSON.stringify(view.toJSON()), /3\/3 files committed/);
```

Observed on `main` `c4f5ecb` (probe run against the same sources):

```
not ok 1 - a directory transfer reports its expanded files as the total
  error: The input did not match the regular expression /3\/3 files committed/.
  Actual rendered row: "3/1 files committed"
# tests 1
# pass 0
# fail 1
```

### Suggested fix (red first)

1. Add the assertion above to `apps/web/tests/AgentActivityPanel.test.tsx` and watch it fail with `3/1`.
2. Change the denominator to the expanded file list: `total: item.progress.length` (a one-line change at `AgentActivityPanel.tsx:103`). `committed` already counts `progress` entries, so both sides then describe the same collection.
3. The test passes with `3/3`; a transfer of a single file stays `1/1`, and a partial transfer reads `2/3`.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- Commit: `main` `c4f5ecb36ca0439d8e45cc30f1e8d0210413ea70` (bug lines re-read there; probe executed on the same sources)
- OS: Linux x86_64 (container)
- Node.js: `v22.23.2`
- pnpm: `11.1.2`
- Command: `node --import tsx --test apps/web/tests/<probe>.test.tsx` from the repository root, after the workspace packages are built
- Relevant packages: `react@19.2.7`, `react-test-renderer@19.2.7`, `tsx@4.23.1`
- No network, no credentials, no real workspace needed: the panel is rendered with a stubbed `ApiClient`.

## Additional Information

- Search before filing: `"files committed"` (5 hits: none is this defect), `"fileProgress"` (0), `"AgentActivityPanel"` (2: #238/#394, a different Session-not-found bug), `"progress.length"` + transfer (0). No open issue or PR covers the transfer row's total.
- The bug is only visible when a mapping expands to more than one file (a directory mapping); single-file transfers read `1/1` and look correct, which is why it survived.
- Related but distinct: #840/#841/#842 are about the artifact preview payload, not the Activity panel.

## Version Information

- `main` at `c4f5ecb36ca0439d8e45cc30f1e8d0210413ea70`
- Web client: `@sciencediscovery/web` workspace package at that commit
- API: `@sciencediscovery/api` workspace package at that commit
- The affected file `apps/web/src/AgentActivityPanel.tsx` is identical at `8708320f80af8a72ea96653e2a71bd89d83a6850` and at `c4f5ecb`
847.title: [Bug]: Activity panel reports a directory transfer as 3/1 files committed

848.author: zhaozhaozz
848.body:
## Problem

CI runs the full selected profile even when a change only touches documentation. Unit tests, system tests, mocked end-to-end tests, coverage, and, outside a pull request, the real end-to-end, binary, and Docker jobs do not inspect those files.

The required status check stays `merge-gate`. A documentation-only change must still be able to merge.

## Documentation-only

A change is documentation-only only when every changed path is one of:

- `README.md`
- `README_zh.md`
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `LICENSE`
- `Third_Party_Open_Source_Software_Notice.txt`
- any path under `docs/`

A rename counts both the old path and the new path. If the changed-file list cannot be determined, do not take the skip path.

Markdown or text outside that list is not documentation-only. In particular, `skills/`, tests, workflows, packages, services, and other product files keep the current CI profile even when the diff is only Markdown.

## Behavior

Apply this decision on `pull_request`, `push`, and `merge_group`.

`workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call` keep the requested profile and do not skip jobs because of the diff.

When the change is documentation-only:

- `policy` still runs.
- The existing documentation check still runs: `pnpm docs:check` (`check:docs`, Markdown lint and documentation link validation).
- Skip CI jobs that this diff cannot affect: the rest of L1 (architecture, catalog, end-to-end metadata, and any other L1 case that is not the documentation check), UT, ST, `e2e-plan`, mocked E2E, coverage, binary, Docker, `real-merge`, and `real-scheduled`.
- `merge-gate` still runs for a non-draft pull request, for push, and for merge group. It passes. It does not fail because those jobs were skipped, and it does not fail because their artifacts are absent.
- The required check name remains `merge-gate`. Do not change repository rulesets.

When any changed path is outside the documentation list, keep today's job selection and today's gate rules.

Draft pull requests already skip the heavy jobs. A documentation-only draft still runs the documentation check, and does not start the skipped jobs above.

## Tests

Add unit tests for the path decision and the gate decision:

- documentation-only diff skips the unaffected jobs and still requires the documentation check and `merge-gate` to succeed
- a mixed diff keeps the current profile
- an unreadable diff does not skip
- `workflow_dispatch` and `workflow_call` do not skip
- `merge-gate` accepts the expected skips only for a documentation-only change; a normal pull request still fails the gate when UT, ST, or E2E is skipped

Run the new tests and the existing CI policy tests. A product end-to-end run is not required for this workflow change.

## Acceptance

- A pull request that changes only `docs/**/*.md` runs the documentation check and `merge-gate`, and skips UT, ST, mocked E2E, and coverage.
- The same skip applies on `merge_group`, including real E2E, binary, and Docker, and `merge-gate` is green.
- A pull request that also changes a source file runs the current profile.
- Existing non-documentation CI behavior stays the same.
848.title: ci: skip unaffected jobs for documentation-only changes

850.author: zhaozhaozz
850.body:
## Background

The CI board for a real end-to-end run is the GitHub Actions run summary. The Nightly workflow (`Nightly`, `.github/workflows/nightly.yml`) calls CI with `profile: daily` and its report job writes only the gate result, the SHA, and the binary artifact names. That is not enough to see how each L5 case actually ran.

L5 is the `release` profile. L4 is the `daily` profile used by Nightly. `test/support/tagged/profiles.mjs` states that every existing eligible real case starts at L3 or L4, so L5 currently selects the same real cases as L4. A table that appears only on a release run would almost never be visible. This issue publishes the same per-case table on both the nightly real E2E run and a release real E2E run.

The shared slice summary (`.ci/tagged-summary.mjs`) stays as it is. Its columns are slice, plan digest, planned, executed, passed, failed, and skipped. This issue adds a separate per-case table. It does not replace that slice summary.

The real E2E score stager (`.ci/prepare-real-e2e-results.mjs`) already keeps `schema_version`, `case`, `case_id`, `integration_status` / `integration`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `generation_duration_ms`, and the numeric evaluation fields (`score`, `total_score`, `baseline_gate_score`, `best_gate_score`, `overall_score`, citation fields, `status`, `gating`). It does not publish peak memory, generated tokens, judge tokens, total tokens, or tool-call counts. Case metrics do fetch session usage (`generation_usage` or `usage`) and then the stager drops it, because raw results can contain model text and credentials. The only per-case table written to the step summary today is the separate, non-gating PUCT review table.

This is not a substitute for #817. #817 remains the coverage, flake-stability, and release-duration issue. This issue does not change which cases run, the gate rules, required check names, or repository rulesets.

## What to build

Publish one markdown table of real E2E case execution details.

Column contract, in this order:

| # | case | status | score | peak memory GB | generated tokens | judge tokens | total tokens | tool calls | duration min |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

- `#` is the execution order, starting at 1.
- `case` is the case id, such as `da-1-3`.
- `status` is the case outcome (`passed`, `failed`, `skipped`, or the recorded `integration_status`). The reference layout shows completed rows only. Failed and unfinished selected cases must stay in the table, so this status column is required.
- `score` is the case's official evaluation score. Prefer `evaluation.overall_score`, then `evaluation.total_score`, then `evaluation.score`. Do not use the non-gating PUCT review score.
- `duration min` is `generation_duration_ms / 60000`, shown to one decimal place. Do not substitute the shard wall clock.
- `generated tokens` is the generator's recorded completion tokens. `judge tokens` is the judge's recorded tokens. `total tokens` is the recorded total. When the usage record has only one total, put that number in `total tokens` and leave the split as `n/a`. Do not invent a split.
- `tool calls` is the recorded tool-invocation count for that case.
- `peak memory GB` is the measured peak RSS of that case, in gigabytes, to two decimals. Record it from the case process when the run can sample it.

Display tokens in compact form (`34.2K`, `14.5M`) when the value is at least 1000, and as an integer below that. A missing measurement is the text `n/a`. Never write `0` or a guessed number in place of a missing measurement.

Row order is `started_at` ascending. A selected case with no `started_at` is still listed, after the timed rows, ordered by case id. The table includes every case selected for that real E2E run, not only successes.

Copy only these numeric and identity cells into the table and the artifact. Do not copy prompts, answers, traces, assertion text, error strings, or secrets, even if they sit beside the measurements in the raw result.

Write the table to:

1. The GitHub Actions job summary of the combined real E2E account step, for `profile: daily` and `profile: release`.
2. A run artifact named `case-execution-details.md` on that same run.
3. The Nightly report summary, so opening the Nightly run shows the table or a direct link to that artifact next to the existing gate line. A release run shows the same table in its real E2E summary and artifact.

The slice summary and the PUCT review table stay unchanged.

## Acceptance

- A nightly run (`profile: daily`) and a release run (`profile: release`) each produce `case-execution-details.md` and show the table in the run summary.
- The header is exactly the columns above, in that order.
- Rows follow `started_at`. Every selected case appears once. A failed case is visible and is not dropped.
- A case that recorded a score and a duration shows those values. A case with no peak-memory sample shows `n/a` in that cell.
- A planted secret or model answer in a fixture result does not appear in the markdown.
- Gate results, the required check name `merge-gate`, and rulesets are unchanged. A missing optional cell does not fail the gate.
- A contract test covers the header, the order, `n/a` for a missing metric, inclusion of a failed case, and the exclusion of secret or model text.

## Out of scope

- Changing L4/L5 case selection, coverage collection, flake retries, or the release duration goal in #817.
- A new web page. The Usage page is not this board.
- Editing gate logic or rulesets.

852.author: moShangLouTou
852.body:
Related to #718 (v0.4.0-rc1 release tracking), specifically the scope to refactor the effective scope of Skills, MCP, and other modules and improve settings/UI consistency.

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] The reported behavior remains in the upstream main implementation checked below (source inspection; no fresh UI reproduction).
- [x] Environment information and minimal reproduction steps are provided below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Desktop and Web use different meanings for prominent MCP/data-source controls even when they share the same backend. Desktop's built-in switches control source permission, while Web's connector selections control which sources a session uses. A built-in source can therefore appear enabled in Desktop while an ordinary session has none of its tools selected. The underlying two-layer behavior is consistent, but the Desktop setting exposes the wrong layer for the intended workflow and makes tool availability difficult to understand.

The intended Desktop system setting is **global default source selection for sessions**, not a per-session editor. Desktop currently has no corresponding per-session settings UI.

#### Minimal reproduction

1. Open Desktop and Web against the same backend with fresh/default settings and no specialist contributing connectors.
2. In Desktop system settings, open **MCP servers** and observe that built-in entries are enabled.
3. In Web global settings or the session connector picker, observe that built-in scientific sources are not selected; only `web` is selected by default.
4. Toggle a built-in source such as PubMed in Desktop, then reload the Web settings. The source's session-selection list does not change.

Actual: Desktop writes `plugins["connector.<sourceId>"].enabled`, while Web selection writes `enabledConnectorIds`. An enabled Desktop source does not automatically provide that source's tools to a session. Conversely, a disabled effective plugin setting can filter out a source that the session has selected.

This is a settings semantics/UX issue, not an exception or crash; there is no relevant stack trace. Steps above describe the reporter's shared-backend scenario and are supported by code inspection, but were not independently rerun in a browser during issue preparation.

#### Expected behavior and acceptance criteria

- [ ] Desktop system settings select **which data sources sessions use by default**, by reading/writing global `enabledConnectorIds`, matching Web global settings. Selecting a source must not merely toggle its plugin permission.
- [ ] Built-in source permission remains allowed by default and is not exposed as the routine source-selection switch. Preserve current default selection (`web` only); being bundled must not automatically select all scientific sources.
- [ ] Changes made in either client are visible in the other after reload. Preserve normal inheritance: global defaults apply to inheriting projects/sessions; explicit project/session selections remain effective.
- [ ] Keep a separate **Enable service** control for custom MCP connection/authentication/tool discovery. Custom sources also participate in global default source selection; enabling their service alone must not select them for sessions. Make the two controls and the new-service default consistent across clients.
- [ ] Use consistent terminology: **Data source** for user-facing selection; **MCP server** for transport/address/authentication configuration; distinguish **Use by default** from **Enable service** and connection readiness.
- [ ] Explain that specialist-provided sources may supplement the session selection and that service readiness/permissions still constrain actual calls. Verify this behavior remains intact.
- [ ] Verify through the supported product entry points that an inheriting ordinary session gains/loses the relevant tool availability when the global selection changes, and that an explicit project/session override is preserved. Cover custom-service disabled/unavailable behavior separately. Do not imply an already-running task is reconfigured live.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Product scenario: Desktop and Web connected to the **same backend**, as confirmed by the reporter.
- Inspection environment: Linux/WSL2, kernel `6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2`, x86_64; Node.js `v22.19.0`; pnpm `11.1.2`.
- No native Windows/macOS Desktop runtime validation or fresh browser journey was performed for this report. The issue concerns configuration semantics shared through the backend, not a demonstrated OS-specific failure.
- External scientific credentials/services are not required to observe the mismatched stored fields. Successful live tool calls require a ready service.

### Additional Information

#### Implementation evidence

- [Desktop MCP settings](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/3fc77a3f0d20f4ff844f572a2ba9772ae4903ea8/apps/desktop/src/views/settings/system/McpServers.tsx#L276): built-in toggles and bulk actions write global connector plugin permissions; display defaults to enabled unless explicitly false.
- [Web source selection](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/0b2479200cf2f94a105e8d33427732266cbbcddb/packages/mcp/src/web.tsx#L12): reads/writes `enabledConnectorIds`.
- [Default selection](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/0b2479200cf2f94a105e8d33427732266cbbcddb/packages/schema/src/runtime-settings.ts#L51): `["web"]`.
- [Effective source filtering](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/0b2479200cf2f94a105e8d33427732266cbbcddb/packages/mcp-sources/src/selection.ts#L4): source selection is filtered by MCP and per-connector plugin settings. `web` is a built-in web capability, not an MCP source.

Source and server are not necessarily one-to-one: multiple built-in sources share the `biomed` MCP server. Avoid presenting a source-selection switch as if it controls that entire transport server.

#### Follow-up discussion: global tool controls (not required to close this bug)

Consider an advanced **Allowed tools** section per source. A useful distinction is global tool prohibition, rather than another selection list: tools are allowed by default, and an explicitly disabled tool cannot be called through Web, Desktop, specialists, or subagents. Source deselection should retain tool preferences. Enforcement must occur at the backend execution boundary as well as tool exposure, rather than merely hiding UI entries. This needs a separate design/implementation decision and should not delay correcting the source-selection semantics.

There are currently no product users requiring an existing-installation settings migration; the reporter explicitly excludes migration work from this request.

### Version Information

- Local source inspected: `main`, `0b2479200cf2f94a105e8d33427732266cbbcddb`.
- Upstream `main` checked during filing: `3fc77a3f0d20f4ff844f572a2ba9772ae4903ea8`. The Desktop MCP file was read at this SHA and still uses the permission switches described above. The shared Web selection/default/filter files linked above were unchanged in the comparison between these SHAs.
- Evidence is source inspection plus the reporter's observations; no test-pass or UI-reproduction claim is made.

## What happens A `.csv` dataset artifact whose version content is **0 bytes** never leaves the loading state in the artifact panel: the launch card is disabled, the raw fold says "Loading CSV Artifact…", and the CSV workspace cannot be opened. The version read has completed successfully — the gate only mistakes an empty document for "not loaded yet". Measured on live `main` `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (Node v22.23.2, `react-test-renderer`), rendering the real `ArtifactModal` with one `.csv` dataset artifact whose version is a 0-byte `text/csv` blob: ```text has-loading: true launch-disabled: true ``` and directly: ```text isCsvWorkspaceReady({ detected: true, loadedVersionId: "v", source: "", versionId: "v" }) === false // expected true ``` The same panel with a one-newline document (`source === "\n"`) is ready, so the zero-byte case is the only one stuck. Zero-byte uploads are an explicitly supported path (`services/api/src/workspace-upload.test.ts:87` "readMultipartUploads keeps zero-byte file parts"), and a 0-byte `.csv` that is later declared as an artifact reaches this code. ## Where - `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:236` — `return detected && Boolean(source) && Boolean(versionId) && loadedVersionId === versionId;` (`Boolean(source)` is the defect; `loadedVersionId === versionId` already proves the version has loaded). - `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:217` and `:222` — `disabled={!ready}` on the launch button and `ready ? :

{t("csv.loadingArtifact")}

`. - `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:570` / `:878` — the panel passes `csvWorkspaceReady` into `CsvArtifactPreview`. - `apps/web/src/ScientificArtifacts.tsx:907` — `csvWindowOpen && artifact && version && csvWorkspaceReady` also keeps the window unmountable. Contrast measured on the same sources: `parseCsvText("\n", …)` throws `CSV must contain a header and at least one data row`, which the workspace shows as an actionable error. The empty document deserves the same treatment, not a permanent spinner. ## Red-first reproduction Add to `apps/web/tests/ScientificArtifacts.test.tsx` (same imports as the existing CSV tests): ```ts test("an empty CSV version is ready once its version has loaded", () => { assert.equal(isCsvWorkspaceReady({ detected: true, loadedVersionId: "version-1", source: "", versionId: "version-1", }), true); }); ``` Run: ```bash cd apps/web node --import tsx --test tests/ScientificArtifacts.test.tsx ``` Observed on `main` `89cd2d30`: ```text not ok 1 - an empty CSV version is ready once its version has loaded error: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true # tests 1 # pass 0 # fail 1 ``` The rendering half is the same failing state: after the version read resolves, the panel text still matches `/Loading CSV Artifact/` and `findAllByType("button").find(csv-artifact-launch).props.disabled === true`. ## Expected result and acceptance - `isCsvWorkspaceReady` must be true once `detected`, `versionId`, and `loadedVersionId === versionId` hold, even when `source === ""`. - The panel must then show a reachable, non-loading state for an empty CSV — either the CSV workspace (whose existing `CSV must contain a header and at least one data row` error is actionable) or an explicit empty-file message. ### Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues for this symptom and found none (terms below).
- [x] I reproduced this on the latest `main` (`89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`).
- [x] This report includes the environment and a minimal reproduction.

### Detailed Description

**What the user sees.** A Session (or a per-message usage line) whose reported token count is just under one million is rendered as `1000K`: the usage chip in the Session header prints `1000K`, the usage page prints `1000.0K` on the chart axis for the same quantity, while the CSV export prints the exact `999999`. The display claims a count (1,000,000) that is not the stored one (999,999), and the unit jumps from `K` to `M` only once the value already crossed the boundary.

**Minimal reproduction** (pure formatter, no DOM):

```ts
import { formatCompactTokenValue } from "./apps/web/src/usageFormat.js";
console.log(formatCompactTokenValue(999_999));   // 1000K
console.log(formatCompactTokenValue(1_000_000)); // 1.0M
```

Observed on `89cd2d30`:

```text
# 999999 -> 1000K
# 1000000 -> 1.0M
```

**Expected.** `999999` renders as `1.0M` (or as an exact `999,999`), never as `1000K`; the compact value must not claim a count the backend did not report.

**Where.** `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:19-21` on `89cd2d30`:

- `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:19` — `if (value >= 1_000_000) return ...M`
- `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:20` — `if (value >= 10_000) return \`${Math.round(value / 1_000)}K\``; for `999_500..999_999` this rounds to `1000`, producing `1000K`.
- `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts:21` — `if (value >= 1_000) return \`${(value / 1_000).toFixed(1)}K\``; same overflow at `999_950..999_999` would produce `1000.0K` if reached.

The same boundary exists in the chart-axis formatter `apps/web/src/UsagePage.tsx:151-152` (`formatChartNumber`), which prints `1000.0K` for the same values.

Consumers: the Session usage chip (`apps/web/src/App.tsx:922` and `:4831`, from `sessionUsage.totals.totalTokens`), per-message usage (`usageInlineLabel`/`usageBreakdownLabel`), and the usage chart axis.

**Red-first fix proposal.** First add a test that fails on `89cd2d30`:

```ts
assert.equal(formatCompactTokenValue(999_999), "1.0M");
```

then cap the `K` branch: if rounding would reach `1_000`, promote to the `M` branch (or floor instead of round), so `999_999` prints `1.0M` and `1_000_000` stays `1.0M`. `formatTokenField` (exact) and the CSV export are untouched. The internal `formatChartNumber` in `UsagePage.tsx` can be fixed the same way; if it is not exported for a direct test, assert it through the rendered chart tick text of a single-day usage page. A second assertion can cover the 1,000-token boundary (`999_999` vs `1_000_000`) as the regression guard.

**Duplicate check (open and closed).** GitHub search: `"1000K"` → 0; `formatCompactTokenValue` → 1 (issue #858, the Usage-page model count, a different bug); `"compact" token` and `token formatting` → only unrelated CI/settings issues. No open or closed issue reports the unit-boundary rounding, and no open PR touches `apps/web/src/usageFormat.ts` except `#811`, which adds `reasoningTokens` to the aggregation (`+4-2`) and does not change `formatCompactTokenValue` (`:17-22` on live main).

### Environment

- Commit: `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0` (live `main`, read 2026-11-04).
- Node `v22.23.2`, pnpm `11.1.2`, Linux x86_64.
- Command: `cd apps/web && node --import tsx --test tests/zz-token-format-probe.test.ts` (temporary probe file, not committed).

### Version Information

- Repository: `openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery`
- `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- Affected package: `apps/web` (`@sciencediscovery/web`)

## Checklist

- [x] I searched existing issues (open and closed) before filing this one.
- [x] This is a defect report, not a feature request.
- [x] I can reproduce it from the code path described below.

## Detailed Description of the Problem

`SessionStore.writeArray` writes a temp file, replaces the target, and removes the temp file in a `finally` block:

```ts
// services/api/src/store.ts:2156-2166
try {
  await writeFile(temporaryPath, `${JSON.stringify(values, null, 2)}\n`, "utf8");
  await renameReplace(temporaryPath, path);   // retries a transient EPERM/EACCES/EBUSY
} finally {
  await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true });
}
```

`renameReplace` classifies an exhausted retry as `FileReplaceError`, which keeps the errno in `code` and the original failure in `cause` so a caller can tell a locked file from a full disk. That classification is lost when the `rm` in the `finally` block itself throws: on Windows an antivirus scanner or an indexer can hold the same fresh temp file that made the replace fail, so `rm` raises a bare `EPERM`, the `finally` throws it, and it replaces the `FileReplaceError` on the way out. The caller then sees an unclassified `EPERM` — exactly the shape this area was just hardened against.

Current vs expected:

- current: replace exhausted → `rm` raises `EPERM` → caller receives a raw `EPERM` (no `FileReplaceError`, no `cause`, no attempt count).
- expected: the classified `FileReplaceError` reaches the caller; the cleanup failure must not substitute for the write failure.

The second half is coverage: the retry-success path asserts no `*.tmp` is left behind (`services/api/src/store-replace.test.ts:60-75`), but the exhausted-failure path has no assertion, so 'the finally still runs' is currently a code-reading claim rather than a checked behaviour.

### Minimal reproduction (red first)

In `services/api/src/store-replace.test.ts`, wrap the same fixture with `context.mock.method(fs, "rename", …)` throwing `EPERM` for every attempt **and** `context.mock.method(fs, "rm", …)` throwing `EPERM`:

```ts
await assert.rejects(() => store.writeArray(sessionId, values), (error) => {
  assert.equal(error.name, "FileReplaceError");          // currently fails: a bare EPERM arrives
  assert.equal(error.code, "EPERM");
  return true;
});
```

Observed now: the assertion fails with `error.name === "Error"` and the message `EPERM: operation not permitted, rm …`. Expected after the fix: `FileReplaceError`. Add a second assertion on the exhausted path that `readdir(sessionRunsDir)` contains no `*.tmp` entry.

### Fix

`services/api/src/store.ts` — the cleanup must not mask the write failure, e.g. `await rm(temporaryPath, { force: true }).catch(() => undefined);`. The retry policy, `FileReplaceError` and the non-transient errno behaviour stay as they are. This is deliberately **not** folded into #816: #816's tip is in review and the change is a separate failure mode.

## Detailed Environment Information Description

- Repository state: `main` at `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- File:line: `services/api/src/store.ts:2156-2166`, existing coverage `services/api/src/store-replace.test.ts:60-75`
- Node: `v22.23.2`; package manager: `pnpm 11.1.2`
- Command for the area: `cd services/api && node --import tsx --test src/store-replace.test.ts`
- Reported by: ScienceDiscovery Security (review of #816 at `82d31f6111ff87be3e2709d7230dd8babc10d507`), filed by ScienceDiscovery Lead

## Version Information

- `main` @ `89cd2d30c93e11c6e98e264cc08b171f6a3705f0`
- Reported 2026-11-04

## Before you start (three constraints on the tests, from a read of the fixtures)

1. **The two acceptances cannot live in one test.** If `rm` is mocked to always throw `EPERM`, the temp file necessarily stays on disk, so a `readdir` assertion that no `*.tmp` remains in the same test can never hold. Split it: **A** = `rm` throws `EPERM`, assert only that the classified error reaches the caller; **B** = `rename` is exhausted while `rm` is the real implementation, assert `FileReplaceError` *and* no `*.tmp` leftover.
2. **The mock needs `syncBuiltinESMExports()`, and the `rm` filter must match the file name, not a substring.** `store.ts:25` imports `rm` as a named ESM binding, and the existing `failReplaces` helper (`store-replace.test.ts:44-55`) is what lets a mock reach the store; without it the mock silently does nothing and the red assertion passes for the wrong reason. Also do not filter on `.tmp`: the fixture root is `<cwd>/.tmp/state-replace-<uuid>` (`store-replace.test.ts:23`) and the teardown calls `rm(root, { recursive: true, force: true })` (`:24`), so a substring filter mocks the teardown too and the test blows up in cleanup. Match `basename` against the `.state-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp` shape written by `store.ts:2156`.
3. **The assertions above do not stop a fake fix.** Asserting only `name`/`code`/no-leftover can be satisfied by wrapping any bare `EPERM` in a hand-built `FileReplaceError` higher up. Add the two cheapest discriminators: `assert.equal(error.attempts, 20)` (and confirm the attempt count with the mock's own counter) and `assert.equal(error.cause.code, "EPERM")`.

A note against over-fixing: the swallowed-cleanup leftover is **inert**. Only two `readdir` calls exist in `store.ts` — `.trash` (`:2103`) and `agent-workspaces` (`:2001`) — and nothing enumerates `session-runs/` or the array directory; `readArray` reads an exact path (`:2147-2153`). So no startup sweep and no retry on `rm` are needed; the fix stays one line plus the tests.
