896.author: moShangLouTou
896.body:
Related to #852 (analogous Desktop MCP settings semantics) and #718 (v0.4.0-rc1 settings consistency and module scope tracking).

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched for related issues but did not get the expected help.
- [x] This bug has not been fixed, as confirmed by the reporter.
- [x] Environment details, reproduction steps, and the boundary between reporter observations and source inspection are provided below.

### 🐞 Detailed Description of the Problem

Desktop **System settings → Skills** exposes individual switches and **Enable all / Disable all**. These controls are intended to manage **global Skill enablement across projects and ordinary conversations**. Instead, the implementation reads and writes the currently active project's Skill selection.

The reporter tested the behavior and confirmed that JiuwenSwarm does not honor the project-level Skill selection. This bug remains unfixed. Desktop writes the wrong configuration scope, and its switches do not provide the intended global control over the Skills used by ordinary conversations.

This is scoped as a **Desktop bug**. Correcting Web's overall Skill management design is not a prerequisite for this issue. However, Desktop must use a coherent backend authority that JiuwenSwarm actually obeys, rather than introduce another disconnected switch.

#### Minimal reproduction

1. Run Desktop with the JiuwenSwarm executor and at least one installed ScienceDiscovery Skill.
2. Select project A and open **System settings → Skills**.
3. Disable an individual Skill, or select **Disable all**.
4. Inspect the saved settings: Desktop updates project A's `skillSelectionMode: "selected"` and `enabledSkillIds`, rather than a global enablement setting.
5. Switch to project B and inspect its Skill state. A system-wide control should not depend on which project was active when it was changed.
6. Start a new ordinary conversation/task and request an operation that requires the disabled Skill. Inspect actual Skill discovery/loading (`skill_tool` / `read_skill`), rather than judging only from the model's answer. The reporter confirmed that JiuwenSwarm ignores the project-level selection. Capture Skill-loading evidence when validating the fix.

Actual: the Desktop controls save project selection instead of global enablement, and JiuwenSwarm does not honor that selection in the reporter's test. The UI does not explain that scope or distinguish the selected list from the executor's own enablement state.

Expected: Desktop's system-level Skill switches control global enablement. Disabling a Skill must prevent newly started ordinary tasks from loading that Skill, regardless of the active project; enabling it restores availability. Availability does not mean every message must automatically execute the Skill.

#### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Individual and bulk switches read/write one authoritative global Skill enablement state. They must not silently modify the active project's selection.
- [ ] The same states are shown after changing projects or reopening settings, and a project need not be active to operate a global control.
- [ ] JiuwenSwarm's effective Skill availability respects the global switches for newly started tasks. A later task must not silently restore a globally disabled Skill through project selection or import/reconciliation.
- [ ] Verify disable, re-enable, and bulk disable across two projects through supported Desktop entry points and actual executor Skill-loading evidence. Include an ordinary conversation without an explicitly attached specialist. Test relevant specialist/subagent paths so they cannot bypass a Skill's global prohibition.
- [ ] Clearly define whether JiuwenSwarm-native builtin Skills are included. If excluded, label the bulk action's scope explicitly; do not imply that disabling the ScienceDiscovery catalog disables every executor Skill.
- [ ] Explain the default enabled set, the treatment of newly installed Skills, and when changes take effect. Keep installed, enabled, loaded, and executed states distinct; do not promise live reconfiguration of an existing task.
- [ ] Avoid competing global/project/executor switches overwriting each other. If project/session selection remains supported, it must operate within global enablement rather than override a global disable.

### Detailed Environment Information Description

- Reporter scenario: Desktop with JiuwenSwarm handling Skills. Exact Desktop build/OS and runtime flags were not supplied in this conversation.
- Source-inspection environment: Linux/WSL2 x86_64; previously recorded Node.js `v22.19.0`, pnpm `11.1.2`.
- No matching local running API/stack process was found during investigation, so the reporter's executor mode and exact settings were not independently inspected.
- No fresh native Desktop/browser reproduction or automated test run was performed for this report. This is not claimed as a Windows/macOS-only failure.
- No exception/stack trace was supplied; the issue concerns setting scope and execution behavior.

### Additional Information

#### Source evidence and investigation boundaries

- [Desktop Skills settings](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/apps/desktop/src/views/settings/SkillsSettings.tsx): loads `getProjectSettings(activeProjectId)` and routes individual/bulk actions through `setEnabledSkills(client, activeProjectId, ...)`.
- [Desktop settings API](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/apps/desktop/src/api/settings.ts): `setEnabledSkills` writes project settings with `skillSelectionMode: "selected"`. Bulk enable pins the current installed list; it is not the dynamic `all` mode.
- [Store settings resolution](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/services/api/src/store.ts): global Skill-selection fields are currently skipped. Merely moving Desktop's existing write to `/api/settings` would not complete the fix.
- [Desktop stack startup](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/scripts/start-stack.mjs): defaults `SCIENCE_AGENT_SKILL_SELECTION` to `desktop`.
- [JiuwenSwarm Skill installation](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts) and [reconciliation](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/blob/f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d/services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-skills.ts): the Desktop-selection mode aligns shared executor switches at task startup, skips JiuwenSwarm `builtin` Skills, and logs reconciliation failures instead of failing the task. This is an investigation lead, not proof of the reporter's exact runtime cause.

Web's JiuwenSwarm controls and Desktop's project selection currently target different state. This explains why comparing the two interfaces alone cannot establish effective enablement. The primary requested correction remains Desktop global semantics and executor enforcement.

The project currently has no product users requiring settings migration; migration is outside the requested scope. This issue is separate from the MCP correction in #852 and does not add MCP tool-level controls to its scope.

### Version Information

- Source inspected: `f060fdfa1d72699ce176fbd32162263d587ba35d`.
- Exact reporter binary/build: not supplied.
- Status: confirmed by the reporter and still unfixed. Source findings and reporter runtime observations are identified separately above.
896.title: [Bug]: Desktop global Skill switches write project settings that JiuwenSwarm ignores

897.author: yuanzhou75
897.body:
Follow-up work for #834 (`feat(sizeopt): slim the Windows installer 797.6 -> ~578.0 MiB, merge 6 envs into 2`). That PR's code is reviewed; this issue carries the parts deliberately left out of it, so they are not only recorded in a review thread.

## 1. Real-machine smoke (the minimum the maintainer asked for)

The full matrix (three install-root lengths timed, bilingual screenshots, 30–60 s recording) was reduced to one smoke pass:

- [ ] One clean Windows machine: install → first launch, with a first-launch timing next to the f26 baseline.
- [ ] Actually trigger the over-long install-root refusal (`win_desktop/build/installer.nsh:306-339`): what the dialog says, and whether choosing "No" really aborts the install instead of continuing into `InstFiles`.
- [ ] One pass through each side of the uninstall "also delete user data" branch (`installer.nsh:541`).

Screenshots or a short written record are enough.

## 2. First-run bytecode completeness

`treeHasPycache` (`win_desktop/src/bootstrap.ts:230-251`) skips the first-run `compileall` as soon as one `__pycache__` directory holds one `.pyc` (`:243`). At the default install root that compile is not runnable anyway — `63 + 1 + 192 + 14 > 259` — so a complete shipped `.pyc` set is load-bearing, and the only place that dependency is written down is the A5 advisory (`assemble-backend.mjs:990-996`), which exists only on the build machine.

- [ ] Write a manifest or count of the precompiled set at assemble time and check it at bootstrap, so an incomplete set (quarantined file, partial copy, interrupted unpack) fails the build or names itself at first launch instead of surfacing as an `ImportError` at first tool use.

## 3. Smaller items raised in review

- [ ] `win_desktop/scripts/after-pack-trim-locales.cjs` hardening (see the #834 review threads for the specific asks).
- [ ] Stale documentation references to the removed per-service `services/<member>/uv.lock` files.

## Not in scope here

- The `uv sync` SIGTERM defect in `scripts/start-stack.mjs` stays in #834: it is a reproducible bug on the current head, not follow-up work.
- The patch-0019 wording in #834's description has been corrected and is accurate on the current head.
897.title: [Follow-up] Windows installer slim (#834): real-machine smoke, first-run bytecode completeness, smaller hardening

898.author: zhaozhaozz
898.body:
## 🚀 Background Description

When the model connection is reset after the model has already streamed part of its answer, the agent run fails. No layer retries it.

That is what ended three research jobs in the manual Nightly run [41852669139](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41852669139) on 2026-11-04 (branch `ci/l5-biomnibench-da`, head `b8819fc8b`, JiuwenSwarm backend, model `deepseek-flash` behind an OpenAI-compatible relay gateway).

### What failed

`research-1` (DRB-58) and `research-5` (DRB-75) both ended with:

```
run_error=[181001] model call failed, reason: openAI API async stream error: APIError: read ECONNRESET
```

The `[model-sse-summary]` lines in each job's `stack.log` (artifact `real-e2e-evidence-<shard>`) identify the request:

| Job | Request sent (UTC) | 200 headers | Connection reset | Streamed before reset | Attempts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| research-1 | 15:00:19.235 | 15:00:23.403 | **15:01:46.872** | 83 s, 848,494 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |
| research-5 | 16:00:31.110 | 16:00:36.449 | **16:03:30.928** | 175 s, 2,791,403 bytes, text and tool calls | 1 |

`research-10` failed in the same way. Its run error reads `interaction round execution failed`, and each of its three failed runs directly follows a mid-stream reset (16:26:31.901, 16:31:37.391 and 16:49:24.951).

### The fault is external; the failure is ours

- 16 of the run's 382 requests to the gateway ended with `error.classification: network`. They came from 5 independent runners, and all of them fall between 15:01 and 16:50 UTC.
- The same gateway served 1,386 requests in the two earlier runs on this branch (03:07–06:38 and 10:09–12:50 UTC) without a single network reset.
- Streams of 176 s / 2.9 MB and 214 s / 2.8 MB completed normally in the same run, so a fixed size or duration limit is not the cause.
- 9 of the 16 resets were retried and recovered. They all came before any answer text or tool-call delta: either before the response opened, or while only reasoning had streamed. The head under test (PR #853) retries the second case.
- The other 7 happened after answer text or tool-call deltas had started. Nothing retried them. Every run failure in research-1, research-5 and research-10 follows one of these 7.

### Retry behaviour on `main` (`48848578`)

On the JiuwenSwarm backend, a model call travels Swarm → ScienceDiscovery model gateway (`services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`) → `packages/model/src/client.ts` → provider.

| Layer | What it retries | After the stream has started |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/model` `requestWithRetry` | Connect errors, header timeout, 429 and 5xx. Budget: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES=2`. Backoff: 0.5 s doubling up to 4 s, or a numeric `Retry-After`. Header timeout: `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600` | Nothing. The code says so: "Once the stream starts flowing, errors surface to the caller". `bodyTimeout: 0` also means a stalled body is never treated as lost |
| JiuwenSwarm model gateway | Nothing of its own. It holds response headers until the first answer byte, so a failure before the stream opens reaches Swarm as a real HTTP error | Forwards the error |
| Swarm's OpenAI SDK | Its built-in retries before a response arrives | Nothing |
| openJiuwen `agent_teams` `StreamController` | — | Re-drives a team member's round that failed with `181001`: up to 10 times, with a "continue" query. The main session run is not covered: research-1 and research-5 logged `run of <session> failed: [181001]` straight after the reset |
| Run | Nothing. `classifyRunFailure` maps ECONNRESET to `transport-error`, which is only displayed and recorded | — |

PR #853 adds one more retry in `streamModelTurn`: `network` and `timeout` errors are retried while `answerStarted` is still false. It cannot cover the 7 resets that came after output had started.

One safety property already holds. The gateway withholds tool-call arguments until the upstream turn finishes; in the meantime it sends empty deltas as progress. A stream cut mid-turn therefore never executes a partial tool call, so re-driving the failed turn cannot repeat a side effect. Text and reasoning deltas, on the other hand, are forwarded as they arrive. That is why the transport layer cannot replay the request transparently once text has started.

### How other agents handle a mid-stream drop

All rows except the DeepSeek API docs were read from current sources.

| Agent | Mid-stream drop | Budget and backoff | Partial output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Codex](https://github.com/openai/codex) | Retries stream disconnects, connection failures, timeouts, 5xx and 429. A stream idle for `stream_idle_timeout_ms` (default 300000) counts as lost | `stream_max_retries` 5 and `request_max_retries` 4. Exponential backoff with jitter; server retry advice wins. After the budget runs out it falls back from WebSocket to HTTPS | Only items completed with `output_item.done` enter history. The retry re-samples from history: the partial item is dropped, completed tool calls are kept |
| [Grok Build](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build) | `StreamError` and `EventStreamError` are retried; `IdleTimeout` is not | 15 retries (`GROK_MAX_RETRIES`). 2 s doubling to 30 s, ±20% jitter. The first retry rebuilds the HTTP client; rate limits are retried once | The same request is re-sampled and the failed attempt is discarded |
| [pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) | Restarts the whole turn at the agent level, matching the error text (`terminated`, `socket hang up`, `other side closed`, `stream ended…`) | 3 retries, 2/4/8 s, capped at 60 s. Shows `Retrying (n/3)` and can be cancelled | The failed assistant message stays in the raw log but is hidden from the model; the agent continues from the previous message |
| [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) | Retries mid-stream errors, including `ECONNRESET` and `ERR_STREAM_PREMATURE_CLOSE` | 3 retries, 1/2/4 s. Failures before the stream opens have a separate policy (5 s up to 30 s) | Emits a `RETRY` event and resends the request |
| [DeepSeek API docs](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/rate_limit) | No agent. 500 and 503: "retry your request after a brief wait". Waiting streams receive `: keep-alive` comments, and the connection is closed if inference has not started within 10 minutes | — | No guidance on mid-stream drops |
| [DeepSeek-TUI](https://github.com/Hmbown/DeepSeek-TUI) (third-party) | Retries only a stream that failed to open. A drop while reading the body is reported and not replayed, to avoid duplicated output | — | — |

The common pattern: retry at the turn, not at the HTTP request. Output counts only once an item or turn completes. On failure, the partial attempt is discarded and the turn is re-sampled from the last committed state, with a bounded, jittered backoff and a visible status.

## Design Ideas

1. **Re-drive the main run's failed turn on a transient transport fault.** This covers a `181001` caused by a network or stream error, or `transport-error`. Drop the failed round from the model's context and continue from the last committed round. openJiuwen already does this for team members, and pi does it for every turn. Budget 3–5 attempts with jittered exponential backoff capped at 30–60 s, honour cancellation, and show a retry status in the run timeline. Still to decide: whether this lives in the JiuwenSwarm patch set or in `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`. The native loop needs the same behaviour.
2. **Treat a stalled stream as lost.** Add an idle timeout on the response body (Codex uses 5 minutes), so a hung stream enters the same recovery instead of waiting forever.
3. **Use a fresh connection on the first retry**, as Grok Build does, so a reset does not reuse a broken pooled connection.
4. **Keep non-transient errors out:** authentication, quota, context-overflow, invalid-request and content-policy errors stay non-retryable.

Alternative, for comparison only: buffer text in the gateway as it already buffers tool calls, so the transport layer can replay the whole upstream request transparently. This would remove live text streaming on the Swarm path.

## Involved Public APIs

This may add settings for the turn retry budget and backoff and for the stream idle timeout, next to `SCIENCE_AGENT_LLM_MAX_RETRIES`. It may also add a run-timeline event for "retrying after a dropped model stream". No change to existing request or session APIs is expected.

## Description of Relevance to Other Modules

- `packages/model/src/client.ts`: retry policy, idle timeout, and the `retryErrors` wire diagnostics.
- `services/api/src/agent-run/jiuwenswarm-model-gateway.ts`, `jiuwenswarm-agent.ts`, the JiuwenSwarm patches, and the native loop.
- Web run timeline: the retry status, and partial text that a retry replaces.
- CI accounting (related to #813): `test/support/tagged/provider-fault.mjs` does not count these failures as provider faults; the run's verdict shows `provider faults 0`. The error text carries no 5xx status, and `PRODUCT_REPORT` (`main run must complete`, `delivery_status`) vetoes it in any case.
- PR #853: the retry it adds for interruptions during the reasoning phase.

## Test Design and Test Plan

- UT for `packages/model` and the gateway: a fake upstream returns 200, streams text and tool-call deltas, then resets the socket. Assert that the turn is re-driven within the budget, that no tool call from the cut attempt executes, and that exhaustion still fails with the original error and wire diagnostics.
- UT: a fake upstream stops sending bytes mid-stream. Assert that the idle timeout classifies the stream as lost and retries it.
- UT: 401/403, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- Mocked E2E: the stub model resets the stream after some answer text. The run completes, the timeline shows the retry, and the answer text is not duplicated.
- Real nightly: wherever `[model-sse-summary]` shows a mid-stream `network` reset, a completed turn follows instead of a failed run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A stream reset after answer text or tool-call deltas have started no longer ends the main run while retry budget remains; the run continues from the last committed turn.
- [ ] No tool call from the interrupted attempt executes, and no completed tool call runs twice.
- [ ] The retry is visible in the run timeline and can be cancelled. When the budget is exhausted, the run fails with the original provider error preserved.
- [ ] Authentication, quota, context-overflow and invalid-request errors are not retried.
- [ ] The JiuwenSwarm and native backends behave the same.
- [ ] A test covering the mid-stream reset fails on current `main` and passes with the change.
- Commands that must pass: `pnpm ci:l1` and `pnpm test:shared`.

## Additional Information

The other failures in run 41852669139 are outside this issue; they come from the head under test, not from the provider:

- `research-6`: none of the 16 evolve expansions produced a runnable candidate. The most common reason logged was that the 16000-token per-call cap was spent on reasoning.
- The mocked `standard-journeys` and `standard-config` workers: the head buffers reasoning deltas until answer text or a tool call starts.

The main scheduled Nightly that day ([41919338127](https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/actions/runs/41919338127), `main` `48848578`, provider called directly) passed, with no network reset in 826 requests.
898.title: [Feature]: Recover an agent run when the model stream drops after output has started

899.author: yuanzhou75
899.body:
## Summary

When the agent calls `ask_user` (for example, the `science-research-team` skill's coarse intent parsing asks the user to pick an analysis goal), the gateway treats the resulting user-input wait as a stall. With no answer within 240 s, the run is failed with:

```
Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms
```

A legitimate "waiting for the user" state should not be subject to the idle-progress watchdog, or should enter a distinct recoverable `waiting`/`blocked` state instead of `failed`.

## Reproduction

1. Start the local stack: `scripts/start-stack.sh --mode local`.
2. Register a working model and make it the default task model.
3. Create a project/session (approvalMode `always_allow`) and upload a CSV to the workspace.
4. Send a deliberately under-specified data-analysis prompt (no analysis goal):
   > 用science-research-team skill去帮我执行一个数据分析任务，需要用的数据是subspace_score_table.csv。
5. The main agent parses intent and calls `ask_user` with a 4-option clarification card ("本次数据分析的目标是什么？…").
6. Leave the question unanswered. After ~240 s the run fails with the stall error.

## Observed behaviour

- `ask_user` tool call at 11:04:47 (local) with a 4-option clarification question.
- No further gateway progress for 240 s (nobody answers in a headless/automated run).
- Run reaches `failed` with `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms` (errorCode `timeout`).

Run evidence (local reproduction):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Session ID | `a8bd3422-0ef1-4e14-a327-0a8a4b18982a` |
| Run ID | `f8b1b2d7-8f97-4744-9680-7d7ca3bf6496` |
| Final status | `failed` |
| Terminal error | `Agent run stalled: no gateway progress for 240000 ms` |

## Expected behaviour

`ask_user` (and the mapped approval / `requestApproval` user-input waits) should suspend or greatly extend the idle watchdog, and ideally surface a `waiting_for_user` / `blocked`-style state that can be resumed when the user answers — not `failed`.

## Environment

- ScienceDiscovery local stack on WSL2 (Ubuntu), JiuwenSwarm backend.
- Model: glm-5.3-flash via an OpenAI-compatible gateway (yibuapi.com/v1).
- Reproduced headlessly by driving `/api/sessions/{id}/messages` and polling `/runs`.

## Relates to

- #819 — same 240 s idle watchdog, different trigger (a hanging `todo_create`). This issue is the complementary case where "no progress" is *expected* because the run is waiting on the user.
899.title: [Bug]: ask_user clarification wait trips the 240s idle watchdog and fails the run
